learningNotes: Use a global access path: An S3 Multi-Region Access Point presents a global endpoint over configured regional buckets and routes supported requests using its service behavior. It does not make every object's data appear in every bucket.

Replicate and authorize separately: Configure supported replication, bucket/MRAP policies, ownership and encryption-key access for the intended requests. Version and replication state still determine which regional data exists.

Control regional failover: Failover controls adjust eligible regional request routing. Prepare destination data and permissions before shifting traffic; a routing change alone is not a complete disaster-recovery plan.
09.decisionCue: Global request routing and regional object replication are separate mechanisms.

09.title: Legacy S3 transforms and Glacier vault retention need context
09.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Understand Object Lambda: The historical Object Lambda pattern transformed supported object responses through Lambda. Availability is now restricted to existing customers and selected partner use; verify eligibility before designing a new workload. Choose a current transform path: For new designs, evaluate an appropriate application/Lambda/API or CloudFront processing path. Transform authorization, caching and latency still need explicit design. Separate Glacier Vault Lock: Glacier vault-service retention policies belong to the historical vault API model. They are different from S3 Object Lock on versioned bucket objects and from selecting an S3 Glacier storage class.
learningNotes: Understand Object Lambda: The historical Object Lambda pattern transformed supported object responses through Lambda. Availability is now restricted to existing customers and selected partner use; verify eligibility before designing a new workload.

Choose a current transform path: For new designs, evaluate an appropriate application/Lambda/API or CloudFront processing path. Transform authorization, caching and latency still need explicit design.

Separate Glacier Vault Lock: Glacier vault-service retention policies belong to the historical vault API model. They are different from S3 Object Lock on versioned bucket objects and from selecting an S3 Glacier storage class.
09.decisionCue: Preserve the old exam concept while selecting a supported current service model.

09.title: Presigned URLs delegate a bounded request
09.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Authorize the signer: A presigned URL represents a particular signed request using the signer's permissions. Scope the operation, bucket/key and required request headers; possession of the URL can grant the intended bearer access. Bound the lifetime: The URL's expiry cannot outlive the usable signing credentials and may be constrained further by policy. Temporary role credentials can expire before a requested URL lifetime. Protect the workflow: Use HTTPS, controlled distribution and appropriate object/size/checksum conditions for the chosen upload mechanism. Test failures and avoid exposing long-lived credentials to the client.

Bound the lifetime: The URL's expiry cannot outlive the usable signing credentials and may be constrained further by policy. Temporary role credentials can expire before a requested URL lifetime.

Protect the workflow: Use HTTPS, controlled distribution and appropriate object/size/checksum conditions for the chosen upload mechanism. Test failures and avoid exposing long-lived credentials to the client.
09.decisionCue: A presigned URL is delegated request authority, not a new public bucket policy.

09.title: S3 evidence: access logs, data events and metrics
09.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Server access logs: Access logging records supported request details to a configured destination. Treat delivery and coverage characteristics as part of the evidence model; it is not a real-time application tracing guarantee. CloudTrail data events: Configure relevant S3 object-level data-event selectors when object API audit is required. Management-event history alone does not automatically record every object read or write. Operational metrics: Request metrics and Storage Lens show aggregate signals at their supported scope and cadence. A metric, an access log and an API audit event answer different questions.
learningNotes: Server access logs: Access logging records supported request details to a configured destination. Treat delivery and coverage characteristics as part of the evidence model; it is not a real-time application tracing guarantee.

CloudTrail data events: Configure relevant S3 object-level data-event selectors when object API audit is required. Management-event history alone does not automatically record every object read or write.
Operational metrics: Request metrics and Storage Lens show aggregate signals at their supported scope and cadence. A metric, an access log and an API audit event answer different questions.
09.decisionCue: Choose evidence by the question: which API, which request, or what aggregate trend?

10.title: EBS is persistent block storage within one AZ
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Attach inside the AZ: An EBS volume is a network block device. Attach it to a compatible EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone; most volumes have one attached instance. Multi-Attach is a specific io1/io2 exception. Reattach or restore: Detach safely and reattach within the same AZ. To move to another AZ, create a snapshot and restore a new volume in the target AZ; a volume itself does not span AZs. Plan persistence and performance: A volume can outlive its instance, depending on Delete on termination. Resize with supported Elastic Volumes operations, extend the OS filesystem, and check the instance EBS bandwidth.
learningNotes: Attach inside the AZ: An EBS volume is a network block device. Attach it to a compatible EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone; most volumes have one attached instance. Multi-Attach is a specific io1/io2 exception.
Reattach or restore: Detach safely and reattach within the same AZ. To move to another AZ, create a snapshot and restore a new volume in the target AZ; a volume itself does not span AZs.

Plan persistence and performance: A volume can outlive its instance, depending on Delete on termination. Resize with supported Elastic Volumes operations, extend the OS filesystem, and check the instance EBS bandwidth.
10.decisionCue: Persistence, AZ scope and attachment rules are separate design decisions.

10.title: EBS: choose the disk for the access pattern
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. General-purpose SSD: gp2 and gp3 balance price and performance for transactional applications, boot disks and general workloads. Provisioned-IOPS SSD: io1/io2 suit sustained IOPS demand. io2 Block Express targets stronger durability and consistent low latency. Throughput-oriented HDD: st1 serves frequent sequential processing; sc1 serves colder throughput workloads. Both exclude boot-volume use.
learningNotes: General-purpose SSD: gp2 and gp3 balance price and performance for transactional applications, boot disks and general workloads.
Provisioned-IOPS SSD: io1/io2 suit sustained IOPS demand. io2 Block Express targets stronger durability and consistent low latency.
Throughput-oriented HDD: st1 serves frequent sequential processing; sc1 serves colder throughput workloads. Both exclude boot-volume use.
10.decisionCue: Choose the access pattern before the volume type.

10.title: gp2 and gp3 separate capacity from performance differently
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Capacity-linked gp2: Smaller gp2 volumes use a credit balance for bursts. Capacity, IOPS and throughput must be evaluated together. Independent gp3 controls: gp3 includes a baseline and permits additional IOPS and throughput within configuration constraints; capacity alone need not buy performance. Consistent io2 performance: Check I/O size, required latency and the complete instance-to-volume path; a published maximum is not an application guarantee.
learningNotes: Capacity-linked gp2: Smaller gp2 volumes use a credit balance for bursts. Capacity, IOPS and throughput must be evaluated together.
Independent gp3 controls: gp3 includes a baseline and permits additional IOPS and throughput within configuration constraints; capacity alone need not buy performance.
Consistent io2 performance: Check I/O size, required latency and the complete instance-to-volume path; a published maximum is not an application guarantee.
10.decisionCue: Capacity, IOPS, throughput and latency are different constraints.

10.title: Find the narrowest point in the EBS path
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Application demand: I/O size and queue depth change the relation between operations per second and transferred bytes. Volume limits: Inspect latency, queueing and throughput alongside provisioned IOPS. A large sequential read behaves differently from small random writes. Instance limits: Use suitable EBS-optimized instances and verify the instance bandwidth/IOPS ceiling before increasing the volume specification.
learningNotes: Application demand: I/O size and queue depth change the relation between operations per second and transferred bytes.
Volume limits: Inspect latency, queueing and throughput alongside provisioned IOPS. A large sequential read behaves differently from small random writes.
Instance limits: Use suitable EBS-optimized instances and verify the instance bandwidth/IOPS ceiling before increasing the volume specification.
10.decisionCue: Measure every link before paying to widen one.

10.title: Snapshots capture changed blocks, not application intent
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Incremental blocks: The first snapshot includes written blocks; later snapshots capture changes. Deleting an earlier snapshot does not automatically invalidate later snapshots. Application consistency: Flush and quiesce appropriately before capture. Detachment is not mandatory; coordinate the database and all related volumes. Managed snapshot storage: Snapshots are EBS-managed recovery resources backed by S3; they are not ordinary objects in a customer-accessible snapshot bucket.
learningNotes: Incremental blocks: The first snapshot includes written blocks; later snapshots capture changes. Deleting an earlier snapshot does not automatically invalidate later snapshots.
Application consistency: Flush and quiesce appropriately before capture. Detachment is not mandatory; coordinate the database and all related volumes.
Managed snapshot storage: Snapshots are EBS-managed recovery resources backed by S3; they are not ordinary objects in a customer-accessible snapshot bucket.
10.decisionCue: A block snapshot is only as application-consistent as its capture procedure.

10.title: Restore in the target AZ and plan first-read latency
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Restore into a new volume: The restored volume must be created in the required AZ and attached to a compatible instance. Initialize the working data: First-read initialization can affect latency after restoring a snapshot. Test startup and application recovery rather than only volume creation. Accelerate deliberately: FSR, manual block reads and provisioned-rate initialization solve different timing/cost needs; their constraints are compared separately.
learningNotes: Restore into a new volume: The restored volume must be created in the required AZ and attached to a compatible instance.
Initialize the working data: First-read initialization can affect latency after restoring a snapshot. Test startup and application recovery rather than only volume creation.
Accelerate deliberately: FSR, manual block reads and provisioned-rate initialization solve different timing/cost needs; their constraints are compared separately.
10.decisionCue: Volume creation is not proof of application recovery readiness.

10.title: Automate recovery points with the right policy service
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Target with tags: DLM policies can target supported instances or volumes and create EBS snapshots or EBS-backed AMIs. Schedule and retain: Creation, retention, deletion and supported copy rules must match recovery and compliance requirements. Choose the governance scope: AWS Backup offers wider supported-service governance; successful backup creation must be followed by restore testing.
learningNotes: Target with tags: DLM policies can target supported instances or volumes and create EBS snapshots or EBS-backed AMIs.
Schedule and retain: Creation, retention, deletion and supported copy rules must match recovery and compliance requirements.
Choose the governance scope: AWS Backup offers wider supported-service governance; successful backup creation must be followed by restore testing.
10.decisionCue: Retention policies are useful only when the recovery points can be restored.

10.title: Encryption needs a working recovery key
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Regional default setting: Encryption by default applies prospectively to new volumes and snapshot copies in that account/Region. Existing data needs migration: Use an encrypted snapshot copy or encrypted new volume from a snapshot, then test and cut over. Enabling the setting does not alter old volumes. Authorize the recovery key: KMS policies and IAM permissions must permit the intended source, destination and recovery principals; cross-account keys need particular care.
learningNotes: Regional default setting: Encryption by default applies prospectively to new volumes and snapshot copies in that account/Region.
Existing data needs migration: Use an encrypted snapshot copy or encrypted new volume from a snapshot, then test and cut over. Enabling the setting does not alter old volumes.
Authorize the recovery key: KMS policies and IAM permissions must permit the intended source, destination and recovery principals; cross-account keys need particular care.
10.decisionCue: Test key access as part of recovery, not after a failure.

10.title: Multi-Attach shares a block device, not a normal file share
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Shared block device: Each attached instance can read and write the same blocks. Multi-Attach is not an NFS/SMB server. Supported attachment scope: Up to 16 supported Nitro instances in one AZ; Linux supports io1/io2, Windows supports io2. Check current instance and driver requirements. Coordinate every writer: Use a cluster-aware filesystem or application and appropriate fencing. Mounting ordinary ext4/XFS concurrently can corrupt data.
learningNotes: Shared block device: Each attached instance can read and write the same blocks. Multi-Attach is not an NFS/SMB server.
Supported attachment scope: Up to 16 supported Nitro instances in one AZ; Linux supports io1/io2, Windows supports io2. Check current instance and driver requirements.
Coordinate every writer: Use a cluster-aware filesystem or application and appropriate fencing. Mounting ordinary ext4/XFS concurrently can corrupt data.
10.decisionCue: Shared blocks require coordinated writers.

10.title: Grow EBS deliberately; treat instance store as disposable
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Resize persistent storage: Supported size/type/performance changes are separate from extending the partition and filesystem in the guest OS. Migrate to shrink: EBS cannot shrink in place. Copy validated data to an appropriately smaller new volume, then perform a controlled cutover. Protect host-local data: Instance-store disks have instance-defined capacity and high local I/O. Use them for recreated scratch/cache; back up or replicate irreplaceable data.
learningNotes: Resize persistent storage: Supported size/type/performance changes are separate from extending the partition and filesystem in the guest OS.
Migrate to shrink: EBS cannot shrink in place. Copy validated data to an appropriately smaller new volume, then perform a controlled cutover.
Protect host-local data: Instance-store disks have instance-defined capacity and high local I/O. Use them for recreated scratch/cache; back up or replicate irreplaceable data.
10.decisionCue: Persist required data beyond the lifetime of its host.

10.title: EFS shares files across clients and AZs
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Managed shared NFS: NFSv4.1 and POSIX semantics suit Linux applications that require concurrent shared-file access; EFS is not native Windows SMB. Regional or One Zone: Regional storage spans AZs; One Zone accepts a single-AZ boundary. File capacity grows automatically, but network and performance planning remain. Choose a file workload: CMS, WordPress, web serving and shared application content are common fits. Pay for used storage and applicable access/throughput features.
learningNotes: Managed shared NFS: NFSv4.1 and POSIX semantics suit Linux applications that require concurrent shared-file access; EFS is not native Windows SMB.
Regional or One Zone: Regional storage spans AZs; One Zone accepts a single-AZ boundary. File capacity grows automatically, but network and performance planning remain.
Choose a file workload: CMS, WordPress, web serving and shared application content are common fits. Pay for used storage and applicable access/throughput features.
10.decisionCue: Choose shared-file semantics and the right failure boundary.

10.title: A mount target is the network doorway to EFS
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Mount-target network path: Allow NFS TCP 2049 between the client and mount-target security groups; verify subnets, routes and return traffic. Keep the path local: Use an available mount target in the client AZ to avoid unnecessary cross-AZ paths. Mount-target availability differs for One Zone. Extend private connectivity: DX/VPN or supported VPC connectivity needs working DNS resolution or explicit target addressing. Provide redundant links and endpoints where required.
learningNotes: Mount-target network path: Allow NFS TCP 2049 between the client and mount-target security groups; verify subnets, routes and return traffic.
Keep the path local: Use an available mount target in the client AZ to avoid unnecessary cross-AZ paths. Mount-target availability differs for One Zone.
Extend private connectivity: DX/VPN or supported VPC connectivity needs working DNS resolution or explicit target addressing. Provide redundant links and endpoints where required.
10.decisionCue: A correct mount needs a working private path in both directions.

10.title: EFS authorization has several independent layers
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Network and IAM gates: Security groups provide reachability. Authenticated NFS mounts use the EFS helper and relevant IAM filesystem/client policies. POSIX file permissions: File UID/GID and directory read/write/execute permissions remain meaningful; IAM authorization does not replace POSIX checks. Access-point identity: Enforce an application root directory and identity. Restrict access-point use in policy; TLS protects transit and KMS protects stored data.
learningNotes: Network and IAM gates: Security groups provide reachability. Authenticated NFS mounts use the EFS helper and relevant IAM filesystem/client policies.
POSIX file permissions: File UID/GID and directory read/write/execute permissions remain meaningful; IAM authorization does not replace POSIX checks.
Access-point identity: Enforce an application root directory and identity. Restrict access-point use in policy; TLS protects transit and KMS protects stored data.
10.decisionCue: Reachability, IAM and POSIX permissions solve different access questions.

10.title: Choose EFS throughput to match demand
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Choose the performance mode: General Purpose is the recommended low-latency mode. Previous-generation Max I/O has higher operation latency and configuration restrictions. Match variable demand: Elastic throughput follows changing demand without requiring stored capacity to purchase throughput. Provision or use credits: Provisioned sets throughput separately from capacity. Bursting earns/spends credits based on Standard-class bytes; read metering differs from writes.
learningNotes: Choose the performance mode: General Purpose is the recommended low-latency mode. Previous-generation Max I/O has higher operation latency and configuration restrictions.
Match variable demand: Elastic throughput follows changing demand without requiring stored capacity to purchase throughput.
Provision or use credits: Provisioned sets throughput separately from capacity. Bursting earns/spends credits based on Standard-class bytes; read metering differs from writes.
10.decisionCue: Choose a throughput mechanism that matches demand.

10.title: EFS lifecycle changes cost and access behavior
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Choose the access tier: Standard serves frequent file access; IA and Archive lower storage cost for less-used eligible files through lifecycle policies. Model the complete cost: Include retrieval/access costs, minimum durations, eligibility and latency. A lower storage rate does not guarantee a lower total bill. Respect the AZ boundary: Regional supports Archive; One Zone has a different class set. Automatic backups and restore readiness must fit the accepted failure boundary.
learningNotes: Choose the access tier: Standard serves frequent file access; IA and Archive lower storage cost for less-used eligible files through lifecycle policies.
Model the complete cost: Include retrieval/access costs, minimum durations, eligibility and latency. A lower storage rate does not guarantee a lower total bill.
Respect the AZ boundary: Regional supports Archive; One Zone has a different class set. Automatic backups and restore readiness must fit the accepted failure boundary.
10.decisionCue: Model access and recovery costs with storage costs.

10.title: EFS replication is asynchronous recovery
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Asynchronous copy: Initial synchronization must finish before the destination data is available. Continued replication is asynchronous. Protected destination: The active destination is protected against application writes; prepare its mount targets, key access and policies before failover. Recover the application: Monitor TimeSinceLastSync and test a deliberate writable failover and client remount. Replication does not preserve an independent backup history.
learningNotes: Asynchronous copy: Initial synchronization must finish before the destination data is available. Continued replication is asynchronous.
Protected destination: The active destination is protected against application writes; prepare its mount targets, key access and policies before failover.
Recover the application: Monitor TimeSinceLastSync and test a deliberate writable failover and client remount. Replication does not preserve an independent backup history.
10.decisionCue: Monitor the recovery point and prove the failover steps.

10.title: Choose FSx by filesystem semantics
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Windows file semantics: Windows File Server: SMB and Active Directory. Parallel compute: Lustre: parallel compute and S3-linked datasets. ONTAP or OpenZFS: ONTAP: NFS, SMB and iSCSI; OpenZFS: managed NFS with ZFS capabilities.
learningNotes: Windows file semantics: Windows File Server: SMB and Active Directory.
Parallel compute: Lustre: parallel compute and S3-linked datasets.
ONTAP or OpenZFS: ONTAP: NFS, SMB and iSCSI; OpenZFS: managed NFS with ZFS capabilities.
10.decisionCue: Start with protocol and application semantics.

10.title: Windows file shares keep Windows access controls
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Native Windows access: SMB with native NTFS semantics supports traditional enterprise shares, home directories and compatible Windows applications. Directory and permissions: Integrate Microsoft AD for authentication and use ACLs, quotas and DFS Namespaces to manage access and file organization. Compatible private clients: Linux needs a compatible SMB client. On-premises access needs private routing, DNS and AD connectivity over supported DX/VPN paths.
learningNotes: Native Windows access: SMB with native NTFS semantics supports traditional enterprise shares, home directories and compatible Windows applications.
Directory and permissions: Integrate Microsoft AD for authentication and use ACLs, quotas and DFS Namespaces to manage access and file organization.
Compatible private clients: Linux needs a compatible SMB client. On-premises access needs private routing, DNS and AD connectivity over supported DX/VPN paths.
10.decisionCue: Windows file access needs both directory and network design.

10.title: Multi-AZ Windows file storage protects the server tier
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Active and standby servers: Managed Multi-AZ deployments keep active and standby Windows file servers in different AZs. Reconnect after failover: Failover changes the serving node; applications must tolerate the interruption and reconnect through supported names. Keep recovery history: FSx-managed automatic daily backups are enabled by default. They preserve recovery history; Multi-AZ alone does not reverse a mistaken delete.
learningNotes: Active and standby servers: Managed Multi-AZ deployments keep active and standby Windows file servers in different AZs.
Reconnect after failover: Failover changes the serving node; applications must tolerate the interruption and reconnect through supported names.
Keep recovery history: FSx-managed automatic daily backups are enabled by default. They preserve recovery history; Multi-AZ alone does not reverse a mistaken delete.
10.decisionCue: Availability replicas and historical backups protect different failures.

10.title: Change Windows file-system layout through migration
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Create the target layout: For a different AZ deployment or smaller allocated filesystem, provision a compatible new target. Copy and validate: Use a supported backup restore or DataSync migration. A backup restore is not a general way to shrink storage; migrate to a smaller target instead. Cut over deliberately: Stage the copy, pause writes, perform final synchronization, validate ACLs/data and switch application paths or DNS aliases.
learningNotes: Create the target layout: For a different AZ deployment or smaller allocated filesystem, provision a compatible new target.
Copy and validate: Use a supported backup restore or DataSync migration. A backup restore is not a general way to shrink storage; migrate to a smaller target instead.
Cut over deliberately: Stage the copy, pause writes, perform final synchronization, validate ACLs/data and switch application paths or DNS aliases.
10.decisionCue: Plan migration and cutover before changing the storage layout.

10.title: Lustre feeds parallel compute
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Parallel shared files: Lustre provides concurrent shared-file access for HPC, ML, video processing, financial modeling and engineering workloads. Compute and storage together: Select storage media and throughput for metadata, small/random I/O or large/sequential I/O; benchmark the parallel workload. Link durable source data: Supported S3 repository linkage enables file processing without making S3 itself a general POSIX filesystem. Private hybrid clients still need supported connectivity.
learningNotes: Parallel shared files: Lustre provides concurrent shared-file access for HPC, ML, video processing, financial modeling and engineering workloads.
Compute and storage together: Select storage media and throughput for metadata, small/random I/O or large/sequential I/O; benchmark the parallel workload.
Link durable source data: Supported S3 repository linkage enables file processing without making S3 itself a general POSIX filesystem. Private hybrid clients still need supported connectivity.
10.decisionCue: Parallel compute needs an appropriate shared-data path.

10.title: Lustre durability depends on deployment and storage type
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Scratch is recreatable: Scratch does not replicate data or replace failed file servers. Keep inputs and valuable outputs independently recoverable. Persistent SSD and HDD: These persistent configurations replicate data within one AZ and replace failed file servers. Plan independent protection for an AZ failure. Persistent Intelligent-Tiering: Current Intelligent-Tiering replicates data across multiple AZs. Data durability and filesystem serving availability are different properties; test application recovery.
learningNotes: Scratch is recreatable: Scratch does not replicate data or replace failed file servers. Keep inputs and valuable outputs independently recoverable.
Persistent SSD and HDD: These persistent configurations replicate data within one AZ and replace failed file servers. Plan independent protection for an AZ failure.

Persistent Intelligent-Tiering: Current Intelligent-Tiering replicates data across multiple AZs. Data durability and filesystem serving availability are different properties; test application recovery.
10.decisionCue: Specify deployment and storage type before describing the failure boundary.

10.title: Lazy loading brings the working set to Lustre
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Import the namespace: Linked S3 metadata can be imported before all file content is present in Lustre. Load data on demand: Reads fetch the needed file data, allowing a job to start without downloading the complete repository; retained working data reduces repeated fetches. Export results explicitly: Configure automatic import/export or explicit repository tasks as supported. Changed output reaches S3 only through the configured export behavior.
learningNotes: Import the namespace: Linked S3 metadata can be imported before all file content is present in Lustre.
Load data on demand: Reads fetch the needed file data, allowing a job to start without downloading the complete repository; retained working data reduces repeated fetches.
Export results explicitly: Configure automatic import/export or explicit repository tasks as supported. Changed output reaches S3 only through the configured export behavior.
10.decisionCue: Import and export behavior must be configured deliberately.

10.title: ONTAP combines file and block protocols
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Serve file and block clients: Storage virtual machines and volumes expose NFS, SMB and iSCSI to compatible Linux, Windows, macOS and application clients. Protect and clone data: Snapshots, replication, efficient clones, compression and deduplication support migration and testing; changed data can consume additional space. Manage storage tiers: Manage SSD capacity, IOPS and capacity-pool tiering separately. Automatic tiering is not unlimited capacity or an unconditional automatic-shrink promise.
learningNotes: Serve file and block clients: Storage virtual machines and volumes expose NFS, SMB and iSCSI to compatible Linux, Windows, macOS and application clients.
Protect and clone data: Snapshots, replication, efficient clones, compression and deduplication support migration and testing; changed data can consume additional space.
Manage storage tiers: Manage SSD capacity, IOPS and capacity-pool tiering separately. Automatic tiering is not unlimited capacity or an unconditional automatic-shrink promise.
10.decisionCue: Tiering, capacity and high availability are separate controls.

10.title: OpenZFS brings ZFS capabilities to managed NFS
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Managed NFS access: OpenZFS exposes supported NFS v3/v4 variants; compatible clients need the right protocol, DNS and network permissions. Snapshots and clones: Point-in-time snapshots and writable clones support data recovery and safe testing. Compression saves space only where data compresses. Provision the failure model: Select Single-AZ or Multi-AZ capabilities, throughput and capacity deliberately. Managed service operations do not replace application-level recovery design.
learningNotes: Managed NFS access: OpenZFS exposes supported NFS v3/v4 variants; compatible clients need the right protocol, DNS and network permissions.
Snapshots and clones: Point-in-time snapshots and writable clones support data recovery and safe testing. Compression saves space only where data compresses.
Provision the failure model: Select Single-AZ or Multi-AZ capabilities, throughput and capacity deliberately. Managed service operations do not replace application-level recovery design.
10.decisionCue: A snapshot, a clone and a deployment choice solve different jobs.

10.title: S3 File Gateway translates file access into objects
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Translate NFS or SMB: On-premises clients use NFS or SMB while the gateway stores file data as S3 objects. Cache before asynchronous upload: Local cache absorbs writes and serves active reads; cloud upload is asynchronous. Size the cache for the working set and dirty data. Monitor object and cache behavior: Watch upload completion and cache pressure. External S3 changes require supported refresh behavior; coordinate writers to avoid object conflicts.
learningNotes: Translate NFS or SMB: On-premises clients use NFS or SMB while the gateway stores file data as S3 objects.
Cache before asynchronous upload: Local cache absorbs writes and serves active reads; cloud upload is asynchronous. Size the cache for the working set and dirty data.
Monitor object and cache behavior: Watch upload completion and cache pressure. External S3 changes require supported refresh behavior; coordinate writers to avoid object conflicts.
10.decisionCue: Local file access and asynchronous cloud durability are separate events.

10.title: Volume Gateway: decide where the primary data lives
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Cached primary in AWS: Cached volumes store primary data in managed AWS storage and retain a local working set. Stored primary on premises: Stored volumes keep the full primary dataset locally and back it up asynchronously to AWS. Recover through snapshots: Both expose iSCSI blocks. Plan local storage/upload buffers, snapshot recovery and connectivity; an EBS snapshot can restore a recovery volume.
learningNotes: Cached primary in AWS: Cached volumes store primary data in managed AWS storage and retain a local working set.
Stored primary on premises: Stored volumes keep the full primary dataset locally and back it up asynchronously to AWS.
Recover through snapshots: Both expose iSCSI blocks. Plan local storage/upload buffers, snapshot recovery and connectivity; an EBS snapshot can restore a recovery volume.
10.decisionCue: Locate the primary data before choosing the gateway mode.

10.title: Tape Gateway preserves the backup interface
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Preserve the tape workflow: Existing compatible backup software writes through an iSCSI virtual tape library rather than replacing its backup workflow. Eject and archive: Online virtual tapes are managed in S3-backed storage; ejected archived tapes use supported Glacier archive destinations with restore timing/cost. Understand legacy alternatives: FSx File Gateway is closed to new customers. Its historical SMB/local-cache design is distinct from S3 File Gateway and current new-deployment choices.
learningNotes: Preserve the tape workflow: Existing compatible backup software writes through an iSCSI virtual tape library rather than replacing its backup workflow.
Eject and archive: Online virtual tapes are managed in S3-backed storage; ejected archived tapes use supported Glacier archive destinations with restore timing/cost.
Understand legacy alternatives: FSx File Gateway is closed to new customers. Its historical SMB/local-cache design is distinct from S3 File Gateway and current new-deployment choices.
10.decisionCue: Keep the tape interface while planning cloud retrieval behavior.

10.title: EBS walkthrough: modify, extend and verify
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Inspect the sandbox volume: Illustrative sandbox: inspect attachment, AZ, encryption, volume type and the instance EBS limits; take an appropriate recovery point. Modify and extend: Choose a supported volume modification. Wait for the required operation state and extend the guest partition/filesystem using OS-specific steps. Verify and clean up: Check lsblk/df and application behavior, validate the recovery point and remove sandbox resources. Never format an existing data volume just to expand it.
learningNotes: Inspect the sandbox volume: Illustrative sandbox: inspect attachment, AZ, encryption, volume type and the instance EBS limits; take an appropriate recovery point.
Modify and extend: Choose a supported volume modification. Wait for the required operation state and extend the guest partition/filesystem using OS-specific steps.
Verify and clean up: Check lsblk/df and application behavior, validate the recovery point and remove sandbox resources. Never format an existing data volume just to expand it.
10.decisionCue: Modify, extend and verify; never replace verification with a success icon.

10.title: EFS walkthrough: mount, authorize and prove sharing
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Create the authorized path: Illustrative sandbox: create a filesystem, suitable mount targets, a narrow TCP 2049 rule and configured application identity/access point. Mount with TLS: Install the EFS helper and mount with TLS plus the intended IAM/access-point options. Replace example IDs and check directory UID/GID permissions. Prove sharing and denial: Write/read a file from two authorized clients. Configure a separate denied policy or directory for the negative test; then unmount and clean up.

10.title: A snapshot, an AMI and a regional recovery copy solve different jobs
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Preserve volume blocks: Snapshots preserve block data; a data-volume snapshot alone is not complete application boot metadata. Define a bootable image: An EBS-backed AMI references snapshots and includes relevant boot characteristics and block mappings. Instance type belongs to the launch decision/template. Prepare regional recovery: Copy snapshots or AMIs before a regional outage, authorize destination-region KMS keys and prove that a recovery instance can launch.

10.decisionCue: An AMI supplies boot metadata; a launch template defines a launch configuration.

10.title: DLM owns the recovery points created by its policies
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Select tagged resources: Choose supported instance/volume targets using the policy's selection rules; custom schedules commonly use tags. Manage policy-created backups: DLM creates and retains snapshots or EBS-backed AMIs and applies configured lifecycle/copy actions. Know the ownership boundary: DLM does not take over arbitrary external snapshots or instance-store-backed AMIs. Wider supported-service governance belongs to AWS Backup.

10.title: Choose file-storage performance without changing its semantics
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Windows SSD or HDD: Windows SSD suits latency-sensitive or metadata-heavy access; HDD can fit suitable sequential, cost-sensitive shares. Lustre I/O pattern: Lustre performance depends on media, throughput and the degree of concurrent compute demand, not just filesystem capacity. Enterprise file features: ONTAP/OpenZFS features preserve their filesystem semantics; select the correct client protocol, connectivity, deployment and protection model.

Enterprise file features: ONTAP/OpenZFS features preserve their filesystem semantics; select the correct client protocol, connectivity, deployment and protection model.

10.title: Deploy a gateway with identity, cache and recovery in mind
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Separate client and bucket identity: S3 File Gateway uses an IAM role for bucket access; SMB can authenticate users through Active Directory. Size gateway resources: File Gateway allocates local disks as cache, including dirty uploads. Separate upload-buffer requirements belong to other gateway types; size resources for the selected type. Choose supported deployment: Choose supported virtual host deployment. The historical AWS hardware appliance is no longer sold, and FSx File Gateway is unavailable to new customers.

Size gateway resources: File Gateway allocates local disks as cache, including dirty uploads. Separate upload-buffer requirements belong to other gateway types; size resources for the selected type.
Choose supported deployment: Choose supported virtual host deployment. The historical AWS hardware appliance is no longer sold, and FSx File Gateway is unavailable to new customers.

10.title: Snapshot capture: protect the application's state
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Coordinate writes: A snapshot captures block storage, not an arbitrary database transaction. Flush writes, pause or quiesce applications as appropriate, and coordinate related volumes. Detach is not mandatory: A volume can remain attached while a snapshot is created. For stronger consistency, use a supported application-consistent procedure rather than assuming every attached snapshot is complete. Schedule around real load: Snapshot activity and application I/O share resources. Plan capture windows, monitor application impact and test restoration before relying on the recovery point.

Detach is not mandatory: A volume can remain attached while a snapshot is created. For stronger consistency, use a supported application-consistent procedure rather than assuming every attached snapshot is complete.

10.decisionCue: Consistency comes from the capture procedure and a tested restore.

10.title: Snapshot initialization: choose the recovery mechanism
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Manual read initialization: Read the restored device's blocks with a supported fio or dd procedure when appropriate. Read into /dev/null; do not overwrite production data during initialization. Fast Snapshot Restore: Enable FSR for the required snapshot/AZ pairs. It has eligibility, performance and volume-creation-credit limits plus additional charges. Provisioned initialization: A supported provisioned initialization rate gives more predictable block-download timing at extra cost. Specifying it overrides FSR for that volume; monitor initialization before application tests.

Fast Snapshot Restore: Enable FSR for the required snapshot/AZ pairs. It has eligibility, performance and volume-creation-credit limits plus additional charges.

Provisioned initialization: A supported provisioned initialization rate gives more predictable block-download timing at extra cost. Specifying it overrides FSR for that volume; monitor initialization before application tests.
10.decisionCue: Compare recovery timing, limits and cost rather than assuming every restored volume is warm.

10.title: EFS access points: give each application its own view
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Enforce identity: Example: application A uses UID/GID 2101 through access point A. EFS can replace the client-supplied POSIX identity with the access-point identity. Override the root: Access point A exposes /app-a as the client root; application B uses a separate /app-b root and identity. Configure directory ownership and permissions correctly. Authorize the entry point: Use filesystem/IAM conditions to restrict the allowed access point and require the intended TLS/IAM mount. An access point does not remove the need for network or POSIX permissions.

Override the root: Access point A exposes /app-a as the client root; application B uses a separate /app-b root and identity. Configure directory ownership and permissions correctly.

Authorize the entry point: Use filesystem/IAM conditions to restrict the allowed access point and require the intended TLS/IAM mount. An access point does not remove the need for network or POSIX permissions.
10.decisionCue: A scoped directory view and an enforced identity complement policy authorization.

10.title: EFS policy defaults: do not confuse network access with IAM
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Understand the default: Without a user-configured filesystem policy, network-reachable anonymous NFS clients are allowed by the default policy. POSIX permissions still apply. Use authenticated mounts: The EFS mount helper with IAM authorization evaluates relevant identity and filesystem policies. ClientMount, ClientWrite and ClientRootAccess represent different permissions. Restrict deliberately: Enforce TLS and the intended principals/access points; configure root access appropriately. Test allowed and denied mounts after policy propagation.

Use authenticated mounts: The EFS mount helper with IAM authorization evaluates relevant identity and filesystem policies. ClientMount, ClientWrite and ClientRootAccess represent different permissions.
Restrict deliberately: Enforce TLS and the intended principals/access points; configure root access appropriately. Test allowed and denied mounts after policy propagation.
10.decisionCue: IAM is an explicit client authorization design, not an automatic replacement for NFS permissions.

10.title: EFS burst credits: connect storage size to throughput
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Earn the baseline: Bursting throughput earns credits according to Standard-class storage. A larger Standard working set can earn a higher baseline; cold-class bytes do not purchase the same baseline. Spend credits on peaks: Unused baseline accumulates credits. Demand above baseline spends them; after depletion, sustained performance follows the available baseline and applicable limits. Separate read metering: Reads are metered differently from writes. Use the exact current formula and Region/client limits in the comparison reference; choose Elastic or Provisioned when the credit model does not fit.

10.title: EFS replication: measure RPO and rehearse RTO
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Finish the initial sync: The initial copy depends on data size and file count; destination data is not available until that sync completes. It is not an instant empty-to-ready recovery. Monitor the recovery point: AWS targets a 15-minute RPO for most filesystems after initial sync, with documented workload exceptions. Track TimeSinceLastSync and the last replicated timestamp. Test the complete failover: A writable destination, mount targets, DNS, KMS/IAM access and application remounts determine practical RTO. Replication uses managed capacity and does not consume the source's provisioned throughput allocation.

10.title: File Gateway data can feed cloud processing
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Upload then process: NFS/SMB clients write through the local gateway to S3. Trigger downstream work only when the intended object/upload is ready; local close alone is not proof of completed cloud upload. Extend the workflow: S3 events can invoke Lambda, while Athena, Redshift Spectrum or EMR consume supported datasets from S3. Handle duplicated events and concurrent changes in the consumer design. Replicate deliberately: Supported S3 replication can move objects to another bucket/Region. Validate versioning, permissions and destination access; replication does not coordinate multiple gateway writers.

10.title: Read-only gateway replicas need refresh and writer discipline
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Choose one writer: Use one authoritative write share for an object set. Multiple gateways writing the same objects can create conflicts; a shared bucket is not a distributed file-lock manager. Expose read-only shares: Other sites can use read-only gateway shares backed by the intended S3 data. Network/file permissions and gateway caching still control what readers see. Refresh the inventory: External changes need supported cache refresh or refresh settings. RefreshCache updates cached object inventory, not a full eager download; wait for completion before validating new files.

10.title: File Gateway backups: lifecycle, versions and WORM
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Tier backup objects: A backup application can write files through the gateway to S3. Apply deliberate Standard/IA/archive lifecycle and retention rules, including retrieval time and minimum-duration charges. Recover a previous version: Versioning can retain overwritten objects. Restore the intended object version through S3, then refresh the gateway inventory so file clients see the recovered state; test the recovery workflow. Retain protected versions: S3 Object Lock protects eligible object versions with retention or legal hold. A client modification can create a new version; it does not rewrite an already protected version.

Recover a previous version: Versioning can retain overwritten objects. Restore the intended object version through S3, then refresh the gateway inventory so file clients see the recovered state; test the recovery workflow.

10.title: Gateway recovery: restore the correct storage interface
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Recover block volumes: Volume Gateway exposes iSCSI. Its cloud snapshot recovery can create an EBS volume for an EC2 recovery workload; adapt the application and validate data consistency. Retrieve virtual tapes: Tape Gateway presents an iSCSI virtual tape library. Ejection and archive change retrieval time and cost; use compatible backup software to retrieve and restore the tape data. Protect the whole path: Use supported encrypted cloud transport over internet or private connectivity. Local cache, upload buffers and host resources depend on gateway type; loss of unuploaded data remains a separate risk.

Retrieve virtual tapes: Tape Gateway presents an iSCSI virtual tape library. Ejection and archive change retrieval time and cost; use compatible backup software to retrieve and restore the tape data.

10.title: Lustre Intelligent-Tiering changes the storage comparison
10.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Elastic storage: Persistent Intelligent-Tiering grows with stored data and moves eligible data among Frequent Access, Infrequent Access and Archive Instant Access tiers. Choose throughput and cache: Throughput is provisioned separately; an optional SSD read cache accelerates eligible reads. This differs from the SSD or HDD capacity-based comparison in older course tables. Keep recovery explicit: Intelligent-Tiering replicates data across multiple AZs. Do not translate that durability feature into an unqualified promise of continuous client access or application disaster recovery.

Choose throughput and cache: Throughput is provisioned separately; an optional SSD read cache accelerates eligible reads. This differs from the SSD or HDD capacity-based comparison in older course tables.

Keep recovery explicit: Intelligent-Tiering replicates data across multiple AZs. Do not translate that durability feature into an unqualified promise of continuous client access or application disaster recovery.

11.title: Choose the database from the access pattern
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Relational transactions: RDS and Aurora serve relational models and SQL workloads. Select engine compatibility, transaction needs and recovery objectives before choosing an instance. Key-based operations: DynamoDB fits known key-based access patterns. Design keys and indexes from queries; a flexible item schema does not create arbitrary relational joins. Specialized access: OpenSearch serves indexed search, DocumentDB compatible document APIs, and time-series engines time-based analysis. A cache accelerates a path without replacing every source-of-truth requirement.

Key-based operations: DynamoDB fits known key-based access patterns. Design keys and indexes from queries; a flexible item schema does not create arbitrary relational joins.

Specialized access: OpenSearch serves indexed search, DocumentDB compatible document APIs, and time-series engines time-based analysis. A cache accelerates a path without replacing every source-of-truth requirement.

11.title: RDS manages the platform while you own the database design
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Select a supported engine: RDS offers supported PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server and Db2 configurations. Engine, version, edition and licensing affect features. Delegate platform work: Managed provisioning, patching, backups and monitoring reduce administration. You still own schema, indexes, query design, permissions and capacity decisions. Scale deliberately: Storage autoscaling can grow eligible storage within configured limits. It does not solve every CPU, connection or query bottleneck, and does not imply automatic storage shrink.

Delegate platform work: Managed provisioning, patching, backups and monitoring reduce administration. You still own schema, indexes, query design, permissions and capacity decisions.
Scale deliberately: Storage autoscaling can grow eligible storage within configured limits. It does not solve every CPU, connection or query bottleneck, and does not imply automatic storage shrink.
11.decisionCue: Managed infrastructure still needs database engineering.

11.title: An RDS connection needs network and database permission
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Prepare the private path: Place databases in an appropriate DB subnet group. Validate routes, DNS, security groups and the engine port from the actual application environment. Keep Lambda connected: A function needs a supported private network path to a private database or proxy. Merely granting IAM permission does not create that path. Separate access gates: TLS protects transport; database authentication identifies the user; database grants authorize SQL operations. Test the complete connection, not only a reachable port.

Keep Lambda connected: A function needs a supported private network path to a private database or proxy. Merely granting IAM permission does not create that path.
Separate access gates: TLS protects transport; database authentication identifies the user; database grants authorize SQL operations. Test the complete connection, not only a reachable port.
11.decisionCue: Reachability, authentication and SQL authorization are separate gates.

11.title: Backups preserve recovery history; replicas serve another purpose
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Use automated recovery: Automated backups and transaction logs support point-in-time recovery within the retained window. Confirm the latest restorable time and retention settings. Retain deliberate snapshots: Manual snapshots remain until deleted and can support eligible cross-account or cross-Region copies. Encrypted copies also depend on usable KMS keys. Restore into a new resource: A successful backup is not a tested restore. Validate data, security settings, endpoints and application cutover on the restored database.

Retain deliberate snapshots: Manual snapshots remain until deleted and can support eligible cross-account or cross-Region copies. Encrypted copies also depend on usable KMS keys.
Restore into a new resource: A successful backup is not a tested restore. Validate data, security settings, endpoints and application cutover on the restored database.
11.decisionCue: Recovery succeeds when the application can use the restored data.

11.title: RDS Multi-AZ and read replicas protect different requirements
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Protect the writer: A classic Multi-AZ DB instance synchronously replicates to a standby in another AZ. The standby supports failover and does not serve ordinary application reads. Scale reads: Read replicas receive asynchronous changes and can serve read traffic. Replication lag matters; eligible cross-Region replicas can support regional recovery. Plan client recovery: Failover and replica promotion change the serving database. Reconnect, refresh DNS appropriately and validate the application rather than assuming existing sessions survive.

Scale reads: Read replicas receive asynchronous changes and can serve read traffic. Replication lag matters; eligible cross-Region replicas can support regional recovery.
Plan client recovery: Failover and replica promotion change the serving database. Reconnect, refresh DNS appropriately and validate the application rather than assuming existing sessions survive.
11.decisionCue: Availability replication and read scaling are different jobs.

11.title: A Multi-AZ DB cluster is different from a classic standby
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Name the deployment: The PDF's non-readable standby describes the classic Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. It does not describe every current RDS Multi-AZ architecture. Use cluster readers: Supported Multi-AZ DB clusters have a writer and two readable instances in three AZs. Check engine, Region, instance and feature compatibility. Keep the distinction useful: Choose the deployment from availability, read scale, failover behavior and cost. A similarly named feature is not evidence of identical replication semantics.

Use cluster readers: Supported Multi-AZ DB clusters have a writer and two readable instances in three AZs. Check engine, Region, instance and feature compatibility.
Keep the distinction useful: Choose the deployment from availability, read scale, failover behavior and cost. A similarly named feature is not evidence of identical replication semantics.

11.title: Replica routing balances connections, not identical query loads
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Select eligible readers: Send read-only work to healthy replicas that satisfy the application's tolerated lag. Keep writes and read-after-write requirements on a suitable path. Understand weighted DNS: Weighted records influence DNS answers. Resolver caching, client connection pools and long-lived sessions prevent an exact per-query traffic split. Monitor the result: Compare replica lag, connection counts and query load. Health checks for private endpoints need a supported monitoring signal rather than direct public probes.

Monitor the result: Compare replica lag, connection counts and query load. Health checks for private endpoints need a supported monitoring signal rather than direct public probes.

11.title: RDS encryption and auditing protect different layers
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Protect stored data: KMS encryption covers supported storage and snapshots. Oracle and SQL Server TDE is a separate engine feature with edition and configuration requirements. Protect the session: Use supported TLS with certificate verification. An encrypted snapshot copy can support migration from an unencrypted source snapshot; plan a tested restore. Observe the right activity: CloudTrail records supported service API actions, not every SQL statement. Enable suitable engine audit or query logs and secure their destinations.

Protect the session: Use supported TLS with certificate verification. An encrypted snapshot copy can support migration from an unencrypted source snapshot; plan a tested restore.
Observe the right activity: CloudTrail records supported service API actions, not every SQL statement. Enable suitable engine audit or query logs and secure their destinations.

11.title: IAM database authentication supplies a short-lived login token
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Prepare both identities: Supported RDS MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL configurations can use IAM database authentication. Configure the database user and the caller's rds-db:connect permission. Connect with TLS: Generate a token for the intended endpoint, port and database user. It is valid for 15 minutes for authentication; use the supported TLS connection path. Retain SQL grants: IAM authentication does not replace database authorization. Token expiry does not itself terminate an already established database session.

11.title: Oracle recovery depends on the destination platform
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Restore to managed RDS: Use supported RDS backup and restore workflows for RDS for Oracle. Managed access differs from a self-managed Oracle host. Export supported RMAN backups: RDS administrative packages can produce supported RMAN backups. Transfer eligible files through S3 for recovery to a compatible self-managed Oracle host; RMAN cannot directly restore an RDS instance. Check engine constraints: RDS for Oracle does not support Oracle RAC. TDE and DMS have their own prerequisites; using Oracle on EC2 transfers more operating responsibility to you.

11.title: A MySQL migration needs a consistent seed and controlled cutover
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Create a consistent export: A supported mysqldump workflow can seed a compatible external MySQL target. Preserve schema objects, character sets and an appropriate consistency strategy. Catch up the target: Where supported, configure replication from the correct binary-log position or GTID state. Monitor errors and lag; a completed file import is not a completed migration. Cut over deliberately: Quiesce writes, verify synchronization and target behavior, then switch the application. Stop or retire replication only after validation and a defined rollback decision.

11.title: RDS Proxy pools connections through a private endpoint
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Reduce connection pressure: Bursty application clients can exhaust database connections. RDS Proxy manages a reusable pool, subject to database capacity and configured limits. Build the private path: The proxy is not publicly accessible. Place it in the database VPC with required subnets, security groups and a reachable client path. Keep application discipline: Use supported IAM or secret-based authentication. Transaction state and session pinning can reduce multiplexing; the proxy does not fix slow SQL or unlimited concurrency.

Build the private path: The proxy is not publicly accessible. Place it in the database VPC with required subnets, security groups and a reachable client path.
Keep application discipline: Use supported IAM or secret-based authentication. Transaction state and session pinning can reduce multiplexing; the proxy does not fix slow SQL or unlimited concurrency.

11.title: Proxy read-only endpoints target eligible Aurora readers
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Separate read and write paths: Use the appropriate proxy endpoint for writer traffic. An additional supported read-only endpoint sends connections to Aurora reader instances. Prepare actual readers: A read-only endpoint needs eligible healthy replicas. Verify permissions, topology and supported engine configuration; an endpoint name does not create a replica. Observe pool behavior: Connection reuse, pinning and reader lag affect the workload. The proxy's read-only routing is different from attaching an RDS proxy directly to an ordinary RDS read replica.

Prepare actual readers: A read-only endpoint needs eligible healthy replicas. Verify permissions, topology and supported engine configuration; an endpoint name does not create a replica.
Observe pool behavior: Connection reuse, pinning and reader lag affect the workload. The proxy's read-only routing is different from attaching an RDS proxy directly to an ordinary RDS read replica.

11.title: Cross-Region RDS recovery requires promotion and application cutover
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Replicate before failure: An eligible cross-Region read replica receives asynchronous changes. Track lag and accept that the latest committed source data may not be present during an outage. Detect and decide: Use an application health route or supported metric/alarm signal to drive a controlled recovery workflow. Avoid promoting solely because one transient probe failed. Recover the serving path: Promote the intended replica, validate data and permissions, then update the application's endpoint or DNS. Fence the old writer and plan later reconciliation.

11.title: Aurora separates database compute from distributed storage

Compatibility does not mean every upstream feature or operational behavior is identical. Share a cluster volume: Database instances use distributed storage replicated across three AZs. Storage growth and reader compute scaling are separate mechanisms. Use current limits: Maximum storage depends on engine version; the PDF's 128 TB figure is not a universal current ceiling. Compare eligible 128 TiB and 256 TiB configurations explicitly.

11.title: Aurora storage replication is different from reader replication
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Protect storage across AZs: Aurora maintains six storage copies across three AZs, with self-healing distributed storage. 11.title: Aurora endpoints select different connection destinations

Use it when a workload needs a particular subset, while retaining other endpoints where appropriate. Instance diagnostics: An instance endpoint addresses one specific instance. Useful for diagnosis, it does not automatically follow a different promoted instance.

11.title: Custom endpoints isolate a deliberate reader workload

11.title: Aurora reader scaling follows demand within configured bounds
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Scale reader compute: Supported Aurora Auto Scaling changes the number of replicas from configured targets and minimum/maximum bounds. 11.title: Aurora logs reveal different kinds of database activity

11.title: Aurora Serverless v2 scales capacity within your chosen range
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Choose a capacity envelope: Serverless v2 adjusts supported database-instance capacity in Aurora Capacity Units within configured bounds. 11.title: The Data API runs SQL over HTTPS with explicit permissions
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Use the service interface: Supported Aurora configurations expose the RDS Data API so clients can execute SQL through HTTPS without managing a persistent database socket. Authorize the request: Grant the required Data API and Secrets Manager access, plus applicable KMS permissions. Database credentials and SQL privileges still exist behind the interface. Match the workload: Check engine/Region support, response-size and transaction constraints. Current Data API support extends beyond the PDF's older Serverless-only description.

11.title: Aurora Global Database separates regional reads from the writer
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Use the primary Region: One primary Region owns the writer. Secondary clusters serve local read workloads using asynchronously replicated storage changes. Plan the current topology: Current supported configurations allow up to ten secondary Regions, with constraints on primary readers and secondary clusters. Do not reuse the PDF's older five-Region limit. Measure recovery: Planned switchover and unplanned failover have different data-loss conditions. Monitor lag, validate eligible versions and rehearse application reconnection.

11.title: Write forwarding still commits changes in the primary Region
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Enter through a secondary: Supported global write forwarding allows an application on a secondary cluster to submit eligible write statements without managing a separate writer connection. Forward to the writer: The primary cluster performs the change first, then replication propagates it. This is not an independent multi-writer database in every Region. Choose consistency behavior: Supported session/read consistency settings affect when secondary reads observe forwarded changes. Cross-Region latency and statement restrictions still apply.

11.title: Move to Aurora through a supported migration path
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Check source compatibility: Eligible RDS engines and versions can migrate using supported snapshot restore or Aurora replica workflows. Validate extensions, parameters and application SQL. Seed and synchronize: A snapshot path creates a new target from a recovery point. A supported replica path can reduce the final catch-up window before promotion. Validate the cutover: Compare data, performance, security and connection settings. Switch applications deliberately and retain the agreed rollback source until validation is complete.

11.title: DynamoDB items use a fixed key and flexible attributes
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Define the table identity: Choose the table's primary-key schema at creation. Each item needs the required key attributes; non-key attributes can vary between items. Use supported values: Scalar values include strings, numbers, binary, Boolean and Null. Lists and maps hold documents; supported set types hold unique scalar values. Respect item limits: An item is limited to 400 KB including attribute names and values. Managed storage growth does not make individual items or request capacity unlimited.

11.decisionCue: Flexible attributes do not remove a deliberate key design.

11.title: Partition and sort keys encode the access pattern
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Distribute partition values: A partition-key-only table requires a unique key per item. Choose a diverse workload key rather than concentrating all requests on one hot value. Group related items: A composite key uses partition key plus sort key; their combination is unique. Items sharing a partition key can be queried in sort-key order. Work an example: Use USER#42 with GAME#101 and GAME#102 for one user's games. Time-oriented sort keys can support ranges when their encoding preserves the required order.

11.title: Query and Scan do different amounts of work
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Query a known partition: A Query uses partition-key equality on a table or index, with an optional supported sort-key condition. Model access patterns around those keys. Treat filters correctly: A filter removes results after items are read. It does not turn a broad read into a cheap key lookup or remove the capacity already consumed. Control scans and pagination: A Scan reads across the target; large results require pagination. Parallel scans increase throughput demand and can compete with production traffic.

Control scans and pagination: A Scan reads across the target; large results require pagination. Parallel scans increase throughput demand and can compete with production traffic.
11.decisionCue: Returning fewer rows does not prove fewer items were read.

11.title: LSIs and GSIs create different alternate access paths
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Local secondary index: An LSI retains the table partition key and changes the sort key. It must be created with the table and shares table capacity. Global secondary index: A GSI can use a different partition key and optional sort key. It can be added later, with its own index capacity behavior and eventual read consistency. Plan projected data: Choose projected attributes, uniqueness assumptions and storage/write cost. Indexes support specified queries rather than unrestricted relational search.

Global secondary index: A GSI can use a different partition key and optional sort key. It can be added later, with its own index capacity behavior and eventual read consistency.
Plan projected data: Choose projected attributes, uniqueness assumptions and storage/write cost. Indexes support specified queries rather than unrestricted relational search.
11.decisionCue: Choose an index from the query and its consistency needs.

11.title: DynamoDB capacity mode changes billing and scaling behavior
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Provision planned capacity: Provisioned mode uses read and write capacity units, with optional Auto Scaling within bounds. Scaling response and hot-key distribution still matter. Use on-demand deliberately: On-demand mode bills for requests and adapts capacity under documented limits. Sudden growth, per-partition limits and configured maxima still need testing. Size actual operations: Read size, consistency and transactional operations affect consumed capacity; writes are rounded by item size. Compare measured demand rather than only request count.

11.title: Choose read consistency for the result the user needs
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Eventually consistent reads: A read can briefly return an older committed version. This is often acceptable for catalogs or feeds and has different capacity cost. Strong reads in supported paths: Strongly consistent reads are available on supported table and LSI operations. GSIs and Streams do not offer strong reads. Separate global semantics: A strong read in an eventually replicated global table does not guarantee the latest write from every Region. Current multi-Region strong consistency is a distinct mode.

11.title: Transactions and conditional writes protect different invariants
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Use a condition for a guard: A supported conditional write can prevent overwriting an unexpected version or consuming an already-used token. Retry logic must handle failed conditions deliberately. Group transactional operations: Transactions can coordinate supported items across tables in one account and Region. Limits, conflict handling and extra capacity cost apply. Keep regional scope clear: Regional transaction atomicity does not make asynchronous global replication transactional across Regions. Multi-Region strong global tables have separate feature restrictions.

11.title: TTL expiration is asynchronous cleanup, not an exact scheduler
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Store the expiry correctly: Use the configured TTL attribute with a numeric Unix epoch value in seconds. An application's date string is not the same representation. Expect delayed deletion: Expired items can remain until DynamoDB removes them. Filter or reject stale records in the application when expiry affects correctness. Observe downstream effects: TTL removals can appear in Streams; replicated deletes and backup retention have separate behavior. TTL is not an authorization boundary or a scheduled job guarantee.

11.title: DynamoDB Streams exposes ordered changes per item
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Choose the record view: Configure keys-only, new image, old image or both images as required. Stream records are retained for 24 hours. Build a resilient consumer: Supported Lambda or custom consumers process changes. Preserve idempotency, retries, partial-failure handling and monitoring. Keep ordering scoped: Changes for one item preserve their sequence; there is no universal order across every table item. A stream is change capture, not the database's permanent backup.

11.title: Kinesis capture extends the DynamoDB change-processing design
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Choose the capture path: DynamoDB can publish item-level changes to Kinesis Data Streams. This differs from consuming the native 24-hour DynamoDB Stream. Set retention and consumers: Kinesis supports configurable retention beyond 24 hours. Account for delivery duplication, ordering considerations and consumer checkpoint/replay behavior. Connect processing and delivery: Use supported Lambda, Managed Service for Apache Flink or Data Firehose integrations to transform and deliver records to destinations such as S3, Redshift or OpenSearch.

Connect processing and delivery: Use supported Lambda, Managed Service for Apache Flink or Data Firehose integrations to transform and deliver records to destinations such as S3, Redshift or OpenSearch.

11.title: Eventually consistent global tables support regional local writes
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Replicate between Regions: Multi-Region eventual consistency global tables accept supported writes in replica Regions and asynchronously propagate changes. Understand conflict behavior: Concurrent updates need a deliberate conflict-aware application design. Regional transactions and strong local reads do not remove replication delay. Separate routing and caching: Route clients to a healthy Region and monitor replication. Cross-Region writes bypass another Region's DAX cache, so cached values can remain stale until refresh.

11.title: Strong global tables use a different replication contract
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Choose MRSC explicitly: Current multi-Region strong consistency synchronously replicates a write to another Region before successful completion. It is distinct from the PDF's asynchronous model. Design the quorum topology: Supported MRSC uses exactly three Regions: three replicas, or two replicas plus a witness. A witness cannot serve application reads or writes. Review feature trade-offs: Region combinations, latency, transactions and TTL support have mode-specific constraints. Test the selected topology rather than treating MRSC as a checkbox on every existing table.

11.title: DynamoDB table classes and backups answer different cost questions
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Choose the table class: Standard and Standard-IA trade request and storage costs differently. Standard-IA remains an online table class; it is not a cold archive requiring restoration. Preserve recovery points: On-demand backups and point-in-time recovery protect against logical damage. Restoration creates a new table; recreate and validate required integrations and application routing. Protect the full design: Check keys, indexes, encryption, IAM, TTL and stream configuration after recovery. Multi-Region replication is not a substitute for historical recovery.

11.title: Index object metadata so the application can query it
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Capture object changes: S3 notifications can invoke processing that records supported object metadata in DynamoDB. Handle duplicate and out-of-order events safely. Design queryable keys: Model customer/date or other access keys and indexes for object lists and date ranges. Store the S3 object reference and required metadata, not oversized payloads. Maintain derived values: A customer's total storage needs a maintained aggregate or a deliberate computation path. A metadata table does not calculate correct totals automatically.

11.title: DAX accelerates supported DynamoDB reads inside a Region
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Cache the hot read path: DynamoDB Accelerator serves eligible cached reads and queries with very low latency. It does not remove write-capacity bottlenecks or every hot-partition problem. Use the DAX client: Applications use a supported DAX-aware client and endpoint. Supported writes through DAX reach DynamoDB and update relevant item-cache behavior. Operate the cluster: Deploy privately with suitable IAM, encryption and monitoring. Production designs typically use at least three nodes across AZs; node count and cache settings remain explicit.

Operate the cluster: Deploy privately with suitable IAM, encryption and monitoring. Production designs typically use at least three nodes across AZs; node count and cache settings remain explicit.

11.title: DAX item and query caches have different freshness behavior
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Select the read path: Strongly consistent reads pass through DAX to DynamoDB rather than being satisfied from the cache. Cached reads use eventual consistency. Understand two caches: An item-cache entry and a cached Query/Scan result are separate. A write-through item update does not automatically repair every previously cached query result. Plan expiry and bypasses: Default TTL is five minutes unless configured otherwise. Writes that bypass DAX, including global-table replication, can leave cached results stale until expiration or refresh.

11.title: DAX and ElastiCache serve different cache contracts
11.imageBrief: Module 09 style. Choose DynamoDB-aware caching: DAX understands supported DynamoDB item and query operations through its client. It is useful when those access patterns dominate. Choose application-managed caching: ElastiCache can hold aggregates, rendered results, sessions and other application-defined values. The application owns serialization, keys and refresh logic. Account for the work: Neither choice removes IAM, network, capacity or failure planning. A computed aggregate in a cache needs a correct invalidation or rebuild path.
