Authorize the backend: Sign management requests with SigV4 and scope execute-api:ManageConnections permissions. The original client token is not an automatic backend IAM permission.
Handle stale connections: A callback can fail with GoneException if the client is gone or not yet established. Remove stale state and implement reconnect/recovery without blind repeated sends.
13.decisionCue: Client WebSocket traffic and backend HTTPS callbacks are different paths.

13.title: AppSync resolvers connect a GraphQL schema to data
13.imageBrief: Module09 style. Define the contract: A GraphQL schema defines available types, fields and operations. Clients request selected fields; schema and resolver logic determine what actually runs. Choose compatible data sources: Supported resolvers can reach DynamoDB, eligible Aurora/Data API paths, OpenSearch, HTTP and Lambda-backed custom behavior. Verify the exact data-source contract. Plan operation and cost: Resolvers need scoped access and valid mapping/runtime behavior. Monitor requests, errors, latency and fan-out; asking for fewer fields does not guarantee fewer backend operations. Diagram: Clientselectedfields->AppSyncschema->3resolverbranches DynamoDB/AuroraviaDataAPI/Lambdacustom, smallerHTTP/OpenSearchsourcecards; avoidcopyingPDFfanoutcomposition.

Choose compatible data sources: Supported resolvers can reach DynamoDB, eligible Aurora/Data API paths, OpenSearch, HTTP and Lambda-backed custom behavior. Verify the exact data-source contract.

Plan operation and cost: Resolvers need scoped access and valid mapping/runtime behavior. Monitor requests, errors, latency and fan-out; asking for fewer fields does not guarantee fewer backend operations.
13.decisionCue: A GraphQL schema describes data; resolvers enforce the real access path.

13.title: AppSync caller authorization and resolver IAM are separate
13.imageBrief: Module09 style. Authenticate the caller: Supported GraphQL modes include Cognito user pools, IAM, OIDC, Lambda and API key. Choose a suitable mode rather than treating an unauthenticated key as private user identity. Authorize fields and tenants: Cognito group rules can distinguish readers from writers. Enforce owner/tenant predicates in resolver/application logic as well as schema-level permissions. Authorize the data source: AppSync resolver roles need scoped backend IAM permissions independently of the caller token. Test negative cross-tenant and forbidden mutation cases. Diagram: CognitoJWTgroups reader/writer->AppSyncfieldauth->resolvertenantpredicate->separatedatasourceIAMgate->DynamoDB. Reader deniedmutation visible.

Authorize fields and tenants: Cognito group rules can distinguish readers from writers. Enforce owner/tenant predicates in resolver/application logic as well as schema-level permissions.
Authorize the data source: AppSync resolver roles need scoped backend IAM permissions independently of the caller token. Test negative cross-tenant and forbidden mutation cases.
13.decisionCue: A valid JWT does not authorize every field or every data item.

13.title: Subscriptions and offline synchronization require different designs
13.imageBrief: Module09 style. Push live changes: AppSync GraphQL subscriptions use secure WebSockets and supported mutation-linked updates. Apply subscription authorization and filtering to avoid exposing another tenant’s events. Recover client state: Offline access/synchronization depends on compatible client libraries, local storage and conflict/version handling. Reconnection may require a fresh query, not just replaying a socket. Distinguish the API product: AppSync Events supplies a separate managed publish/subscribe event API. It is not the same schema/resolver contract as GraphQL subscriptions; old MQTT illustrations are not a universal current protocol. Diagram: Mutation->GraphQLsubscription->connectedclient; offlineclientlocalcache->reconnectquery+conflictcheck; separateAppSyncEvents pub/sub card notschemamutation.

Recover client state: Offline access/synchronization depends on compatible client libraries, local storage and conflict/version handling. Reconnection may require a fresh query, not just replaying a socket.

Distinguish the API product: AppSync Events supplies a separate managed publish/subscribe event API. It is not the same schema/resolver contract as GraphQL subscriptions; old MQTT illustrations are not a universal current protocol.
13.decisionCue: Live transport, durable history and offline conflict resolution are separate.

13.title: Choose an HTTP front door by policy, limits and operating model
13.imageBrief: Module09 style. ALB with Lambda: An ALB can route compatible HTTP requests to Lambda targets alongside other target groups and supported WAF controls. Its event/size/response contract differs from API Gateway. API Gateway or function URL: API Gateway offers product-specific API controls. A Lambda function URL exposes a simpler HTTP endpoint with supported IAM or public access configuration; validate its own permissions and limits. Choose the full path: Compare API features, auth, network exposure, payload, latency, scaling and cost. A direct AWS integration may avoid compute; a custom HTTP backend may need private connectivity. Diagram: Decisionmatrix3cards ALBhybridrouting/APIGatewayAPIfeatures/functionURLsimplerendpoint; bottomdirectAWSbranch. No universalcheaperorcapabilityclaims.

API Gateway or function URL: API Gateway offers product-specific API controls. A Lambda function URL exposes a simpler HTTP endpoint with supported IAM or public access configuration; validate its own permissions and limits.

Choose the full path: Compare API features, auth, network exposure, payload, latency, scaling and cost. A direct AWS integration may avoid compute; a custom HTTP backend may need private connectivity.
13.decisionCue: The simplest front door is the one that still meets every requirement.

13.title: A regional API needs a separate regional data and recovery plan
13.imageBrief: Module09 style. Duplicate the right layers: A multi-Region design needs compatible API deployments, function releases, identity configuration, dependencies and secrets in each intended Region. Choose data behavior: Replicate or recover data using the chosen datastore’s actual consistency and failover model. Avoid two uncontrolled writers during an incident. Test traffic recovery: Validate custom domains, certificates, routing, health checks and client DNS/reconnect behavior. An edge-optimized endpoint still has a regional API behind it. Diagram: TwoRegionboundaries eachAPI+Lambda+regionaldata, deliberatedatareplicationarrow, DNStrafficselectorhealthseparate; noDNSdatabasepromotionclaim.

Choose data behavior: Replicate or recover data using the chosen datastore’s actual consistency and failover model. Avoid two uncontrolled writers during an incident.
Test traffic recovery: Validate custom domains, certificates, routing, health checks and client DNS/reconnect behavior. An edge-optimized endpoint still has a regional API behind it.
13.decisionCue: Global DNS or an edge entry point is not a complete regional recovery design.

13.title: Lambda walkthrough: prove asynchronous failure retention
13.imageBrief: Module09 style. Prepare the sandbox: Use a disposable function, least-privilege execution role and supported failure destination. Set bounded retry/age values and record the test event identifier. Run a controlled failure: Submit an asynchronous test invocation. The accepted response proves intake only; inspect handler logs and configured retry behavior. Verify and clean up: Find the retained invocation record, validate its event identifier and check delivery-failure metrics. Restore normal code, remove temporary resources and confirm no unexpected invocations continue. Diagram: Illustrative sandboxthreepanels configuration, accepted202notcomplete, failurearchiveeventidmatchinglogs. No claimactualAWSaccountwasexecuted.

Run a controlled failure: Submit an asynchronous test invocation. The accepted response proves intake only; inspect handler logs and configured retry behavior.

Verify and clean up: Find the retained invocation record, validate its event identifier and check delivery-failure metrics. Restore normal code, remove temporary resources and confirm no unexpected invocations continue.

13.title: Lambda walkthrough: isolate a private-network timeout
13.imageBrief: Module09 style. Start with evidence: In a disposable VPC-attached function, capture the request ID and exact failed dependency. Separate a private RDS connection from a public HTTPS request. Inspect the right path: Check DNS, subnet routes, security groups, NAT/EIP/IGW or the service endpoint, plus relevant IAM and database grants. A public subnet alone is not a fix. Retest and remove changes: Make the smallest justified configuration correction and rerun the same bounded request. Confirm success with logs and dependency evidence, then remove sandbox-only rules/resources. Add only RDS ingress; retest and remove sandbox rule. NAT is never on the private RDS path.

Inspect the right path: Check DNS, subnet routes, security groups, NAT/EIP/IGW or the service endpoint, plus relevant IAM and database grants. A public subnet alone is not a fix.

13.title: API walkthrough: distinguish throttling from a malformed response
13.imageBrief: Module09 style. Create two controlled cases: In a sandbox API/Lambda integration, use distinct request identifiers for a bounded throttle test and an intentionally invalid proxy-response shape. Read correlated evidence: For an API Gateway stage-throttle 429, inspect stage limits and confirm rejected requests did not invoke Lambda. For 502, inspect integration logs and the REST Lambda proxy response contract. Verify the specific correction: Apply an appropriate throttle/capacity or response-shape change, retest the same case and remove temporary settings. Preserve redacted before/after evidence. Read correlated evidence: For an API Gateway stage-throttle 429, inspect stage limits and confirm rejected requests did not invoke Lambda. For 502, inspect integration logs and the REST Lambda proxy response contract.

13.title: AppSync walkthrough: prove allowed and denied data access

13.title: Identify who invokes Lambda and who retries the work
13.imageBrief: Module09 style. Wait for selected synchronous triggers: API Gateway, an ALB or a direct SDK call can wait for a function result. Separate push-source delivery: S3, SNS and EventBridge can submit asynchronous events. Supported IoT rule and CloudWatch Logs subscription integrations have source-specific permission and payload contracts; source delivery and handler processing are separate. Recognize poll-based processing: SQS, Kinesis and DynamoDB Streams use supported event source mappings that poll and batch records. Their checkpoint, visibility and retry behavior differs from Lambda’s asynchronous queue. learningNotes: Compare runtime, trigger, location, network/file/body, memory and execution quota; avoid older fixed numeric limits unless verified.
Feature support and trigger placement drive selection more reliably than stale quota snapshots.
15.decisionCue: Feature support and trigger placement drive selection more reliably than stale quota snapshots.

15.title: Edge code use cases and cache-key normalization
15.imageBrief: Functions: URI/header transforms, redirects, token checks, cache-key normalization. Lambda@Edge: body, origin logic, network, libraries.
learningNotes: Functions: URI/header transforms, redirects, token checks, cache-key normalization. Lambda@Edge: body, origin logic, network, libraries.
Normalize before cache lookup to avoid unnecessary cache variants.
15.decisionCue: Normalize before cache lookup to avoid unnecessary cache variants.

15.title: Authentication at the edge
15.imageBrief: Viewer token validation at viewer request, protected origin via OAC or origin controls; distinguish function denial and origin authorization.
learningNotes: Viewer token validation at viewer request, protected origin via OAC or origin controls; distinguish function denial and origin authorization.
An edge auth check must validate signature, expiry, audience and policy, not only decode a token.
15.decisionCue: An edge auth check must validate signature, expiry, audience and policy, not only decode a token.

15.title: User-Agent content adaptation
15.imageBrief: Inspect User-Agent or supported device hints and rewrite URI for mobile image, avoiding cache collisions; origin may hold variants.
learningNotes: Inspect User-Agent or supported device hints and rewrite URI for mobile image, avoiding cache collisions; origin may hold variants.
Cache key must vary with transformed resource identity, or users may receive the wrong variant.
15.decisionCue: Cache key must vary with transformed resource identity, or users may receive the wrong variant.

15.title: Global application and dynamic API path
15.imageBrief: CloudFront distributes static S3 content and accelerates dynamic API requests; Lambda@Edge logic can modify routing; DynamoDB access is through application API, not direct edge cache.
learningNotes: CloudFront distributes static S3 content and accelerates dynamic API requests; Lambda@Edge logic can modify routing; DynamoDB access is through application API, not direct edge cache.
Do not treat dynamic application data as static cached content without an explicit policy.
15.decisionCue: Do not treat dynamic application data as static cached content without an explicit policy.

15.title: Lambda@Edge origin selection
15.imageBrief: Origin-request Lambda@Edge on cache miss may select a different configured S3 origin; permissions, DNS/host header and cache behavior matter.
learningNotes: Origin-request Lambda@Edge on cache miss may select a different configured S3 origin; permissions, DNS/host header and cache behavior matter.
Origin-request selection runs only when CloudFront forwards to origin.
15.decisionCue: Origin-request selection runs only when CloudFront forwards to origin.

15.title: CloudFront, Global Accelerator and Route 53 selection
15.imageBrief: DNS routing, HTTP CDN cache and TCP/UDP anycast acceleration solve different layers; combine when architecture calls for them.
learningNotes: DNS routing, HTTP CDN cache and TCP/UDP anycast acceleration solve different layers; combine when architecture calls for them.
A DNS response is not itself an edge content cache or packet proxy.
15.decisionCue: A DNS response is not itself an edge content cache or packet proxy.

15.title: Cache update and observability workflow
15.imageBrief: Versioned asset path, cache-policy TTL, invalidation and cache-hit/error metrics; inspect logs and origin response when stale or failing.
learningNotes: Versioned asset path, cache-policy TTL, invalidation and cache-hit/error metrics; inspect logs and origin response when stale or failing.
Prefer versioned asset URLs for repeatable releases; invalidate when a stable URL must change.
15.decisionCue: Prefer versioned asset URLs for repeatable releases; invalidate when a stable URL must change.

15.title: Walkthrough: private S3 via CloudFront OAC
15.imageBrief: Create private S3 origin and OAC, scope bucket policy, use viewer controls, test CloudFront success and direct S3 denial, clean up.
learningNotes: Create private S3 origin and OAC, scope bucket policy, use viewer controls, test CloudFront success and direct S3 denial, clean up.
Test both allowed distribution access and denied direct origin access.
15.decisionCue: Test both allowed distribution access and denied direct origin access.

15.title: Walkthrough: ALB origin failover and error path
15.imageBrief: Configure primary/secondary origin group, failover status, GET test, ALB origin control and error response; verify POST does not fail over.
learningNotes: Configure primary/secondary origin group, failover status, GET test, ALB origin control and error response; verify POST does not fail over.
Origin group failover eligibility and direct-origin restriction must be tested separately.
15.decisionCue: Origin group failover eligibility and direct-origin restriction must be tested separately.

15.title: Walkthrough: Global Accelerator regional failover
15.imageBrief: Create standard accelerator, listener, endpoint groups and healthy ALBs; test stable IPs and region failure, monitor new-connection rerouting, cleanup.
learningNotes: Create standard accelerator, listener, endpoint groups and healthy ALBs; test stable IPs and region failure, monitor new-connection rerouting, cleanup.
Static anycast IPs remain while endpoint selection responds to health.
15.decisionCue: Static anycast IPs remain while endpoint selection responds to health.

17.title: Choose the security question first
17.imageBrief: Independent service tiles grouped by question: activity, configuration, vulnerability, threat, sensitive data, investigation. No sequential arrows between alternatives.
learningNotes: CloudTrail records API activity; Config records resource configuration
Inspector finds software vulnerabilities and network exposure
GuardDuty detects suspicious activity; Macie discovers sensitive S3 data
Security Hub prioritizes issues; Detective supplies investigation context
Match the question to its evidence source.
17.decisionCue: Match the question to its evidence source.

17.title: Amazon Inspector: coverage before findings
17.imageBrief: Three resource branches enter Inspector, then findings branch to Security Hub and EventBridge. Scan eligibility is a gate before assessment.
learningNotes: EC2: supported packages and network reachability
ECR: supported image OS and application packages
Lambda standard: dependency vulnerabilities; optional code scanning: application code
Coverage status, supported runtimes and exclusions determine what was assessed
Check coverage before interpreting an empty finding list.
17.decisionCue: Check coverage before interpreting an empty finding list.

17.title: EC2 scanning: agent and snapshot paths
17.imageBrief: EC2 has two alternative inventory paths: SSM agent to Inspector, or eligible EBS snapshot to Inspector. Both lead to package findings. Distinct configuration-analysis line for reachability.
learningNotes: Agent-based scanning uses Systems Manager inventory on supported instances
Hybrid mode can use EBS snapshots for eligible unmanaged instances
Network reachability analysis is separate from package inventory
Check scan mode, coverage, permissions, exclusions and last scan time
Agentless scanning has eligibility and permission requirements.
17.decisionCue: Agentless scanning has eligibility and permission requirements.

17.title: Image and function scans follow the artifact
17.imageBrief: Left lifecycle: ECR image digest → scan → rebuild → new digest. Right lifecycle: Lambda code and layers → scan → update → rescan. Independent paths.
learningNotes: ECR enhanced scanning uses Inspector with repository filters and rescan settings
Lambda standard scans dependencies; code scanning adds supported code checks
Deployment, updates and relevant new vulnerabilities can trigger reassessment
Rebuild or update the artifact, deploy it, then verify the new resource coverage
Scanning reports risk; your release process delivers the fix.
17.decisionCue: Scanning reports risk; your release process delivers the fix.

17.title: Prioritize and close a vulnerability
17.imageBrief: Risk inputs feed prioritization, then owner remediation and verification loop. Include finding version and resource identity.
learningNotes: Combine severity with exploitability, exposure and business impact
Assign owner and remediation deadline; record accepted exceptions
Patch EC2 or rebuild images and functions through controlled deployment
Verify the affected version is gone and the finding state is updated
A patched build must reach the running workload.
17.decisionCue: A patched build must reach the running workload.

17.title: AWS Config records the resource story
17.imageBrief: Resource changes on a horizontal timeline create configuration items in Config; an aggregator receives data from two account/Region boxes.
learningNotes: A recorder captures supported resource configuration and relationships
Recording scope, resource types and Region determine visibility
Config rules evaluate compliance against desired configuration
An aggregator centralizes recorded data; it does not turn on remote recorders
A central view depends on recording at the source.
17.decisionCue: A central view depends on recording at the source.

17.title: Configuration history and API history
17.imageBrief: Aligned rows: configuration state, compliance result and CloudTrail API event. Match times with vertical guides, no claim that every change has a human caller.
learningNotes: Config history shows what a resource looked like and when it changed
Compliance history shows rule evaluation results over time
CloudTrail supplies recorded API activity for investigation
Correlate resource ID, Region, principal and timestamps before attributing a change
Use Config state and CloudTrail activity together.
17.decisionCue: Use Config state and CloudTrail activity together.

17.title: Config rules: managed, Lambda or Guard
17.imageBrief: Three equal alternative rule cards, all point to compliance evaluation. Example desired properties: approved volume type or allowed instance family.
learningNotes: Managed rules provide AWS-maintained evaluations
Custom Lambda rules implement supported logic in a function
Custom Policy rules use Guard policy language
Scope and trigger settings determine which resources are evaluated
Custom Config rules are not limited to Lambda.
17.decisionCue: Custom Config rules are not limited to Lambda.

17.title: Detective and proactive evaluations
17.imageBrief: Left before-deployment resource properties → proactive evaluation result. Right deployed change → detective evaluation result. A separate deployment control gate is clearly labeled separately.
learningNotes: Detective evaluation checks deployed resource configuration
Triggers can be configuration changes or periodic evaluations, depending on rule
Supported proactive rules evaluate supplied properties before deployment
Evaluation results do not themselves deny an API request
Assessment and enforcement are different controls.
17.decisionCue: Assessment and enforcement are different controls.

17.title: Remediate safely with Systems Manager
17.imageBrief: Config NON_COMPLIANT → current-state check → SSM Automation → resource change → Config re-evaluation. Failure branch to operator.
learningNotes: A noncompliant result can start a configured SSM Automation runbook
Grant a scoped execution role and validate current resource state
Use retries, exception handling and approval for disruptive changes
Re-evaluate and retain execution evidence after the change
Recheck current state before acting on an older evaluation.
17.decisionCue: Recheck current state before acting on an older evaluation.

17.title: Logs answer different investigation questions
17.imageBrief: Central investigation case surrounded by six evidence cards. Small destination labels: S3, CloudWatch Logs or Firehose as applicable. No claim all logs support every destination.
learningNotes: CloudTrail: API activity; Config: configuration history
VPC Flow Logs: network flow metadata, not packet payload
Load balancer, S3 and CloudFront access logs: request evidence
Route 53 public query logs and Resolver query logs cover different DNS paths
Select the needed log type and enable its delivery path.
17.decisionCue: Select the needed log type and enable its delivery path.

17.title: GuardDuty foundational threat detection
17.imageBrief: Three foundational data inputs feed GuardDuty, then a finding card for suspicious API or network behavior. No customer log bucket prerequisite.
learningNotes: Analyze CloudTrail management events, VPC flow metadata and DNS activity
Threat intelligence, anomaly detection and behavioral signals create findings
Foundational monitoring uses service data streams without your own trail or flow-log export
This detection path needs no workload agent; Runtime Monitoring is separate
Detection data and customer-retained audit logs serve different needs.
17.decisionCue: Detection data and customer-retained audit logs serve different needs.

17.title: GuardDuty protection plans extend coverage
17.imageBrief: GuardDuty center with distinct plan branches: data activity, runtime agent, malware scan. Label optional capabilities; do not depict all plans as agentless.
learningNotes: S3 data access, EKS audit, RDS login and Lambda network activity add signals
Runtime Monitoring uses a security agent for eligible compute workloads
Malware protection examines supported EBS, S3 or backup data paths
Enablement, default settings, Region support and resource coverage must be checked
Verify each protection plan and its resource coverage.
17.decisionCue: Verify each protection plan and its resource coverage.

17.title: Turn a finding into an owned response
17.imageBrief: GuardDuty finding → EventBridge. Branch to SNS notification and controlled response workflow; workflow includes evidence, approval and containment.
learningNotes: A finding describes observed suspicious behavior and affected resources
EventBridge can route matching findings to SNS, Lambda or an orchestration workflow
Enrich with resource context; preserve evidence before containment
Approve high-impact actions and verify the result; a finding alone does not block traffic
Detection requires a response owner and tested action.
17.decisionCue: Detection requires a response owner and tested action.

17.title: GuardDuty across accounts and Regions
17.imageBrief: Organizations management account designates security account; security account manages members in two Region columns. No implied global activation.
learningNotes: The management account designates a member as delegated administrator
Trusted access and service permissions enable organization administration
Account enrollment and protection-plan coverage require explicit management
GuardDuty is regional: verify every target account and Region
Delegation does not prove complete regional coverage.
17.decisionCue: Delegation does not prove complete regional coverage.

17.title: Security Hub and Security Hub CSPM
17.imageBrief: Two linked panels: CSPM posture findings → Security Hub prioritization; Inspector and GuardDuty also feed Security Hub. Clearly label current service names.
learningNotes: Security Hub CSPM evaluates controls and security posture
Security Hub correlates security issues to prioritize exposures and response
Findings from services such as Inspector and GuardDuty add context
Enablement and administration differ between the two services
Posture checks and issue prioritization complement each other.
17.decisionCue: Posture checks and issue prioritization complement each other.

17.title: CSPM control checks need recording
17.imageBrief: Decision split: both services → service-linked recorder; CSPM alone → configure Config recorder. Both lead to control evaluations and findings.
learningNotes: Most AWS CSPM controls use Config rules and resource recording
With both Security Hub and CSPM, a service-linked recorder is created
With CSPM alone, configure the required Config recording yourself
Check account, Region, resource coverage and permissions before trusting results
Recording prerequisites depend on the enablement path.
17.decisionCue: Recording prerequisites depend on the enablement path.

17.title: Aggregate findings without losing scope
17.imageBrief: Two member accounts in two Regions publish findings to a designated aggregation view. Show enablement required at each source, and a separate administration control line.
learningNotes: Service integrations publish findings with resource and source context
CSPM central configuration and aggregation have distinct roles
Cross-Region aggregation does not enable detection in linked Regions
Track severity, workflow state, owner and evidence links
An aggregated dashboard is only as complete as its sources.
17.decisionCue: An aggregated dashboard is only as complete as its sources.

17.title: Security automation needs an exit test
17.imageBrief: Finding → filter → context check → approval where needed → action → verification. Separate failure path to manual handling.
learningNotes: Filter events by source, finding type and resource scope
Use a scoped role and idempotent actions with retry handling
Require approval for disruptive isolation or access changes
Verify control state, record evidence and route failures to an owner
Closing a ticket is not verification of the control.
17.decisionCue: Closing a ticket is not verification of the control.

17.title: Amazon Detective: investigate relationships
17.imageBrief: Behavior graph with principal, IP, EC2 resource and finding connected by labeled observed activity. Time-window selector below; no unsupported accusation labels.
learningNotes: Detective organizes activity into behavior graphs and visual context
CloudTrail, VPC flow data and GuardDuty context support investigations
Pivot across principal, IP address, resource and time window
Correlate evidence before deciding the root cause and containment scope
A graph supplies context; an investigator validates the conclusion.
17.decisionCue: A graph supplies context; an investigator validates the conclusion.

17.title: Amazon Macie: discover sensitive S3 data
17.imageBrief: S3 objects → Macie discovery → sensitive-data finding → EventBridge → controlled response. Show IAM/KMS access gate before content analysis.
learningNotes: Macie inventories supported S3 buckets and discovers sensitive data
Managed identifiers and custom identifiers find selected data patterns
Automated discovery and scoped discovery jobs have different coverage
Findings route through EventBridge and integrations for response
Sensitive-data discovery depends on object accessibility and scope.
17.decisionCue: Sensitive-data discovery depends on object accessibility and scope.

17.title: Macie coverage, identifiers and remediation
17.imageBrief: Two finding lanes: bucket access posture and sensitive content. Both feed triage; remediation changes S3/IAM, not the classifier itself.
learningNotes: Choose buckets, prefixes, sampling and schedule to fit the question
Validate supported formats, storage classes, encryption and key access
Distinguish bucket policy findings from sensitive-content findings
Restrict exposure through approved S3 and IAM changes, then verify
No sensitive-data finding does not prove every object was analyzed.
17.decisionCue: No sensitive-data finding does not prove every object was analyzed.

17.title: Compare the security evidence services
17.imageBrief: Six independent service cards grouped by purpose, with correct official icons and explicit question labels. No pipeline arrows between alternatives.
learningNotes: Inspector: vulnerable software or network exposure
GuardDuty: suspicious activity; Macie: sensitive S3 data
Config and CSPM: configuration posture and controls
Detective: investigation; Security Hub: issue prioritization
Combine complementary evidence rather than choosing one universal scanner.
17.decisionCue: Combine complementary evidence rather than choosing one universal scanner.

17.title: Findings and security data for investigation
17.imageBrief: Parallel security findings response workflow and Security Lake ingestion of supported logs, events and findings; normalized OCSF records in S3 with authorized subscriber access.
learningNotes: A finding summarizes a detected issue with resource and severity context
Security Lake centralizes supported security logs, events and findings in a data lake
OCSF normalizes supported records; Lake Formation governs subscriber access
Retain CloudTrail and service logs according to your evidence requirements
Choose the data product needed for response or investigation.
17.decisionCue: Choose the data product needed for response or investigation.

17.title: Audit evidence and AWS assurance reports
17.imageBrief: Two distinct folders: customer control evidence via Audit Manager; provider assurance via Artifact. Both support audit review, no certification stamp.
learningNotes: Audit Manager organizes control evidence from supported sources and manual uploads
An assessment report packages selected evidence for review
Artifact provides AWS and eligible third-party assurance reports and agreements
Customer compliance still requires scope, operating procedures and reviewer judgment
Evidence collection does not certify the workload.
17.decisionCue: Evidence collection does not certify the workload.

17.title: Data residency is an end-to-end constraint
17.imageBrief: Approved Region boundary contains app, data, logs and backups. Cross-boundary export arrow passes a labeled policy and service-configuration gate to a blocked destination.
learningNotes: Select allowed Regions for data, replicas, backups, logs and recovery copies
Map service processing locations, global endpoints and cross-Region integrations
Use policy guardrails plus service configuration and tested transfer controls
Include support access, keys, metadata and third-party processors in the review
A Region condition alone is not a complete residency design.
17.decisionCue: A Region condition alone is not a complete residency design.

17.title: Threat modelling begins at trust boundaries
17.imageBrief: Generic logical data flow: external User to Public API, Worker and Data store inside application account boundary. Worker has separate external vendor API branch. Threats attach to flows; this is not an AWS deployment topology.
learningNotes: Identify assets, actors, entry points and sensitive data flows
Draw trust boundaries across internet, account, VPC and external service edges
Ask how identity, data integrity, disclosure or availability can fail
Assign mitigations, owners, test cases and residual-risk decisions
Every important boundary needs a threat and a tested mitigation.
17.decisionCue: Every important boundary needs a threat and a tested mitigation.

17.title: Work a data-export threat scenario
17.imageBrief: Scenario diagram with role → S3 sensitive data → external destination. Red dashed attempted export and separate prevention, detection and response annotations.
learningNotes: Threat: stolen role credentials read sensitive objects and export data
Prevent: scoped roles, data access policy and approved destination controls
Detect: CloudTrail data events, GuardDuty signals and Macie classification context
Respond: preserve evidence, revoke sessions or restrict access, then validate
Classification, access prevention and threat detection are separate controls.
17.decisionCue: Classification, access prevention and threat detection are separate controls.

17.title: Least privilege for security automation
17.imageBrief: Two roles: investigator can read evidence; remediator changes only scoped resources. Event validation precedes role assumption and actions.
learningNotes: Read-only investigation and state-changing remediation need different roles
Scope actions to resource tags, accounts and supported resource ARNs
Protect automation against untrusted event fields and confused-deputy paths
Log execution, require approvals where needed and test denied paths
A response system should not become a new escalation path.
17.decisionCue: A response system should not become a new escalation path.

17.title: Access Analyzer: reason about access
17.imageBrief: Resource policy → Access Analyzer → exposure finding. Separate CloudTrail activity evidence card. Clearly distinguish potential access from recorded use.
learningNotes: External access findings examine supported resource policies and trust
Internal and unused access capabilities answer different permission questions
Validate policies and review public or cross-account exposure
A policy finding does not prove that a principal actually used the access
Possible access and observed activity require different evidence.
17.decisionCue: Possible access and observed activity require different evidence.

17.title: AI security evidence and human oversight
17.imageBrief: AI application orchestrator has independent model, authorized retrieval and tool branches. Human approval precedes scoped tool execution; protected audit evidence receives application and tool activity.
learningNotes: Record supported model and agent API activity and scoped application telemetry
Protect prompts, outputs, retrieval data and invocation logs as sensitive data
Apply content safeguards, tool permissions and approval for high-impact actions
Correlate security signals with application evidence and data-retention policy
Model safeguards do not replace tool authorization or audit evidence.
17.decisionCue: Model safeguards do not replace tool authorization or audit evidence.

17.title: An organization security architecture
17.imageBrief: Organizations management designates separate delegated security tooling account. Workload findings feed Security Hub and owned response; customer audit logs independently feed protected S3 archive.
learningNotes: Delegate security administration and retain workload ownership
Enable regional detection and configuration coverage across accounts
Centralize findings, retain protected logs and route owned responses
Measure coverage, detection, remediation and evidence freshness separately
Measure coverage as well as finding counts.
17.decisionCue: Measure coverage as well as finding counts.

17.title: Walkthrough: Config rule to verified correction
17.imageBrief: Five clearly labeled stages: record, evaluate, inspect, remediate, verify. Illustrative compliance transition NON_COMPLIANT → COMPLIANT only after re-evaluation. No fabricated AWS execution claim.
learningNotes: Record the target resource and enable a relevant Config rule
Introduce a controlled noncompliant configuration in a lab
Inspect evaluation timestamp and current state before remediation
Run approved Automation, re-evaluate and retain execution evidence
A fresh evaluation must confirm the correction.
17.decisionCue: A fresh evaluation must confirm the correction.

17.title: Walkthrough: Inspector finding to deployed fix
17.imageBrief: Illustrative single EC2 package example: vulnerable v1, Inspector finding, approved patch/test, corrected v2, rescan and finding review.
learningNotes: Confirm affected resource, package version, scan coverage and exposure
Select a fix or documented mitigation and test it
Patch or rebuild, deploy the corrected artifact, then verify the running version
Review rescan and finding status; retain release and exception evidence
Verify the deployed version rather than only the build result.
17.decisionCue: Verify the deployed version rather than only the build result.

17.title: Walkthrough: investigate suspicious credentials
17.imageBrief: GuardDuty finding leads to CloudTrail/Detective evidence correlation and expected-versus-suspicious decision; preserve evidence before controlled containment and validation.
learningNotes: Review finding details, principal, resource, Region and event times
Correlate CloudTrail activity and Detective context with the expected workflow
Preserve evidence and choose proportionate credential or access containment
Check sessions, permissions and workload recovery after response
Investigate context before making a disruptive identity change.
17.decisionCue: Investigate context before making a disruptive identity change.

17.title: Walkthrough: sensitive data in an exposed bucket
17.imageBrief: Two inputs: access-policy evidence and Macie sensitive-data finding merge into triage → approved access correction → denied unauthorized test plus allowed intended access. Illustrative lab only.
learningNotes: Confirm bucket access posture and Macie discovery scope separately
Review object classification and authorized business access
Restrict unintended access with approved S3/IAM controls
Retest access and classification coverage, preserve evidence and notify the owner
Verify both reduced exposure and intended application access.
17.decisionCue: Verify both reduced exposure and intended application access.

18.title: Choose the AI service by input and outcome
18.imageBrief: Independent input-to-outcome service cards, not a sequential pipeline.
learningNotes: Images and video → Rekognition; documents → Textract
Speech → Transcribe; text to speech → Polly; languages → Translate
Text insight → Comprehend; conversation → Lex and Connect
Custom models → SageMaker AI; foundation models → Bedrock
Choose the data modality and output first.
18.decisionCue: Choose the data modality and output first.

18.title: Rekognition analyzes visual media
18.imageBrief: Image/video source branches into labeling, moderation, face analysis and video tracking.
learningNotes: Image and video labels, objects, scenes and text
Face detection, analysis, search, comparison and celebrity recognition
Video person tracking/pathing and content moderation have separate APIs
Identity verification needs consent and a threshold appropriate to the risk
A detected face is not a verified identity.
18.decisionCue: A detected face is not a verified identity.

18.title: Moderation threshold and human review
18.imageBrief: Confidence axis with automatic allow, review and flag decisions; explain threshold calibration.
learningNotes: DetectModerationLabels returns labels at or above MinConfidence
Lower threshold yields more candidates and more false positives
A human-review range or sample can resolve uncertain cases
A2I remains for existing customers; new designs need another review workflow
A confidence score is evidence for a review policy, not a verdict.
18.decisionCue: A confidence score is evidence for a review policy, not a verdict.

18.title: Transcribe converts speech into text
18.imageBrief: Audio waveform → language identification → ASR transcript → optional PII-redacted output.
learningNotes: ASR creates a transcript from audio
Automatic language identification helps multilingual input
PII redaction is an optional configured output control
Captions, contact-center analysis and searchable media are use cases
Protect both the audio and the transcript.
18.decisionCue: Protect both the audio and the transcript.

18.title: Polly speaks, lexicons pronounce
18.imageBrief: Plain text and SSML inputs merge into Polly; optional pronunciation lexicon alters speech output.
learningNotes: Text or supported SSML → synthesized speech
Pronunciation lexicons map unusual names and acronyms to spoken forms
SSML can control emphasis, phonemes and pauses, subject to voice support
Attach a lexicon to SynthesizeSpeech; test the selected voice and engine
Lexicon controls pronunciation; SSML controls supported speech behavior.
18.decisionCue: Lexicon controls pronunciation; SSML controls supported speech behavior.

18.title: Translate localizes content
18.imageBrief: Source text → Translate → localized text → reviewer → published content.
learningNotes: Amazon Translate converts text between supported languages
Use cases include websites, applications and document text
Check source language, target support, terminology and human quality review
Translation is distinct from speech recognition and speech synthesis
A localized release still needs domain and cultural review.
18.decisionCue: A localized release still needs domain and cultural review.

18.title: Lex and Connect serve different roles
18.imageBrief: Caller → Connect flow → Lex intent → Lambda fulfillment → CRM; escalation branch back to human agent.
learningNotes: Connect receives calls and runs contact flows
Lex recognizes spoken or typed intent with ASR and NLU
A fulfillment step may invoke Lambda and CRM integration
Route unresolved requests to an agent with context and permission boundaries
Connect manages the contact center; Lex interprets the conversation.
18.decisionCue: Connect manages the contact center; Lex interprets the conversation.

18.title: Comprehend finds meaning in text
18.imageBrief: Document and email inputs → Comprehend capability cards; outputs include language, entities, sentiment, syntax and topics.
learningNotes: Detect language, entities, key phrases and sentiment
Syntax analyzes tokens and parts of speech
Topic modeling groups collections of documents
Analyze customer messages with privacy and quality checks
NLP outputs require interpretation in business context.
18.decisionCue: NLP outputs require interpretation in business context.

18.title: Clinical text needs PHI controls
18.imageBrief: Clinical sources → protected text processing → medical entities and PHI findings → authorized reviewer.
learningNotes: Comprehend Medical extracts medical entities and relationships from clinical text
DetectPHI identifies protected health information in supported text
Notes, discharge summaries, test results and narratives are source examples
S3, transcribed speech and streaming ingestion need scoped access and review
Detection does not replace healthcare governance.
18.decisionCue: Detection does not replace healthcare governance.

18.title: SageMaker AI model lifecycle
18.imageBrief: Data → training → evaluation → deployment → monitored predictions → retraining loop.
learningNotes: Prepare labeled training data and select features
Train and tune a model; evaluate on held-out data
Deploy to appropriate inference mode, monitor drift and retrain
Separate experiment permissions, data access, model artifacts and endpoint access
Training accuracy alone does not establish production quality.
18.decisionCue: Training accuracy alone does not establish production quality.

18.title: Forecasting: legacy service and current path
18.imageBrief: Legacy Forecast path beside current SageMaker Canvas/Amazon SageMaker AI path, both consume time-series; no implied migration automation.
learningNotes: Historical time-series plus related features can predict demand
Forecast is closed to new customers; existing customers can continue
For new work, assess SageMaker Canvas time-series or SageMaker AI
Avoid historical percentage-improvement or delivery-time guarantees
Preserve the forecasting requirement while checking service availability.
18.decisionCue: Preserve the forecasting requirement while checking service availability.

18.title: Kendra search and knowledge retrieval
18.imageBrief: Existing Kendra index retrieval versus new Bedrock Knowledge Base retrieval; distinguish search results from generated answers.
learningNotes: Index documents and supported connectors for natural-language search
Rank results using relevance, freshness and feedback controls
Kendra is closed to new customers; existing deployments remain
New solutions can evaluate Bedrock Knowledge Bases for RAG
Search returns evidence; generation creates an answer from it.
18.decisionCue: Search returns evidence; generation creates an answer from it.

18.title: Personalize recommendations
18.imageBrief: S3 history and real-time events feed Personalize; recommendation API serves web, mobile, email/SMS applications.
learningNotes: Historical interactions and item metadata train recommendations
Real-time events update user context; API serves tailored items
Websites, mobile apps and outreach channels consume results
Evaluate cold-start behavior, consent, bias and relevance
Recommendations require data quality and an evaluation metric.
18.decisionCue: Recommendations require data quality and an evaluation metric.

18.title: Textract extracts document structure
18.imageBrief: Document image → Textract → typed structured fields → review → application.
learningNotes: PDF or image input → text, handwriting, tables or form fields
Expense and identity document APIs target specialized structures
Store raw documents and extracted outputs under separate access controls
Validate low-confidence fields before downstream decisions
OCR text and structured field extraction are different outputs.
18.decisionCue: OCR text and structured field extraction are different outputs.

18.title: Managed AI service comparison
18.imageBrief: Four clusters of independent services with official icon labels and precise input/output pairs.
learningNotes: Rekognition, Textract, Transcribe, Polly and Translate solve distinct modalities
Comprehend and Comprehend Medical analyze different text domains
Lex/Connect handle conversations/contact routing
Personalize, Kendra, Forecast and SageMaker AI solve recommendations/search/forecast/custom ML
Do not substitute one AI service merely because it contains ML.
18.decisionCue: Do not substitute one AI service merely because it contains ML.

18.title: Foundation model request path
18.imageBrief: Client → app role → Bedrock runtime → selected foundation model → response; separate optional guardrail and logging controls.
learningNotes: Application invokes an allowed Bedrock model using IAM and regional access
Choose a model and inference profile based on capability, latency, cost and residency
Input and output safeguards are configured explicitly
CloudTrail API activity differs from optional prompt/output invocation logs
Model access, content safety and audit logging are separate settings.
18.decisionCue: Model access, content safety and audit logging are separate settings.

18.title: RAG ingestion and retrieval are separate
18.imageBrief: Top ingestion lane S3 documents → chunk/embedding → knowledge base. Bottom user query → retrieve → prompt with sources → model answer/citation.
learningNotes: Ingestion reads approved source documents, chunks and embeds content
Index stores vectors and metadata with update and deletion lifecycle
Query embeds/retrieves relevant passages before model answer generation
Permissions and citations should correspond to the retrieved source
A prompt cannot retrieve a document that was never indexed.
18.decisionCue: A prompt cannot retrieve a document that was never indexed.

18.title: Knowledge Base choices and access
18.imageBrief: Two knowledge-base architecture options as alternatives; permissions at ingestion and query boundaries.
learningNotes: Managed Knowledge Base manages indexing and retrieval infrastructure
Customer-managed variant gives more control over vector store and parsing
Connector, ACL-filtering and feature support vary by type and Region
Scope data-source role, encryption, network path and retrieval caller
Validate document-level authorization before exposing answers.
18.decisionCue: Validate document-level authorization before exposing answers.

18.title: RAG freshness and answer reliability
18.imageBrief: Source version → sync → retrieval → grounded response; stale-index and no-evidence branches to correction/abstention.
learningNotes: Source updates require ingestion/synchronization and index verification
Handle stale, missing, conflicting and unauthorized passages explicitly
Evaluate retrieval relevance and grounded answer quality separately
Return a safe no-answer or escalation when evidence is insufficient
A fluent answer is not proof of current source grounding.
18.decisionCue: A fluent answer is not proof of current source grounding.

18.title: Bedrock guardrails at inference
18.imageBrief: User prompt → input policy gate → model → output policy gate → app; separate IAM gate for access.
learningNotes: Input and output checks can use configured content and sensitive-information policies
A blocked input prevents usable model inference; output policy can mask/block response
Guardrails do not grant access to tools, data or models
Embedding and reranking models are outside this guardrail path
A guardrail complements authorization; it does not replace it.
18.decisionCue: A guardrail complements authorization; it does not replace it.

18.title: Model invocation logs and data protection
18.imageBrief: Bedrock runtime branches optional invocation logs to same-Region CloudWatch Logs/S3; CloudTrail API activity separate.
learningNotes: Invocation logging is disabled by default and configured per account/Region
Supported bedrock-runtime calls can log request, response and metadata
Same-account/Region CloudWatch Logs or S3 destination and permissions are required
Retain, encrypt and restrict prompts and outputs as sensitive data
Logging content creates another sensitive data store.
18.decisionCue: Logging content creates another sensitive data store.

18.title: AI service permission boundaries
18.imageBrief: Three roles: application caller, knowledge-base ingestion role, reviewer; arrows only for authorized actions.
learningNotes: Caller needs only selected API/model, resource and data access
Service roles for ingestion and vector store access differ from end-user authorization
KMS permissions and private networking may be prerequisites
Test denied paths across accounts, Regions and unsupported resources
Scope the identity for each stage of the data flow.
18.decisionCue: Scope the identity for each stage of the data flow.

18.title: Choose the pattern for the request
18.imageBrief: Four independent pattern cards with example, data need, operational control and failure mode.
learningNotes: Fixed AI API for specialized extraction, speech or vision
SageMaker AI for trained/custom predictive models
Bedrock direct inference for foundation-model tasks
RAG when grounded private knowledge and citations are needed
Start with the required output and evidence boundary.
18.decisionCue: Start with the required output and evidence boundary.

18.title: Walkthrough: media moderation review
18.imageBrief: Media → labels/confidence → threshold branch → review or decision → recorded outcome.
learningNotes: Upload approved media and invoke Rekognition moderation
Set threshold using measured false positives and misses
Route uncertain results to an available human-review workflow
Preserve decision, model version and reviewer outcome
Test policy thresholds with representative content.
18.decisionCue: Test policy thresholds with representative content.

18.title: Walkthrough: accessible contact bot
18.imageBrief: Caller → Connect → Lex → Lambda/CRM; low-confidence branch → human agent.
learningNotes: Connect accepts the call and Lex identifies intent
Lambda validates booking request and checks authorized CRM record
Fulfill or transfer to a human with relevant context
Inspect transcript handling, fallback rate and call outcome
Fallback is part of the designed customer journey.
18.decisionCue: Fallback is part of the designed customer journey.

18.title: Walkthrough: extract invoice fields
18.imageBrief: Invoice → Textract tables/forms → validation rule → reviewer when needed → approved record.
learningNotes: Place source in protected storage and invoke Textract
Extract line items, totals and form keys with confidence
Validate mismatches and review ambiguous fields
Store approved structured output with traceable document version
Do not post an invoice solely because OCR returned text.
18.decisionCue: Do not post an invoice solely because OCR returned text.

18.title: Walkthrough: grounded internal answer
18.imageBrief: Approved document → index; query → authorized retrieval → cited answer, with abstain branch.
learningNotes: Sync an approved document into the knowledge base
Query with caller authorization and retrieval filters
Provide retrieved passages to the model and return source references
Test an absent document, stale version and unauthorized query
Evaluate retrieval and generation separately.
18.decisionCue: Evaluate retrieval and generation separately.

18.title: Walkthrough: train and deploy a model
18.imageBrief: Dataset → train → evaluate gate → deploy → predictions → monitoring.
learningNotes: Prepare labeled data with training/validation split
Train, tune and compare against a baseline
Deploy to suitable endpoint or batch inference path
Monitor performance and trigger retraining with approval
Only a validated model should reach an endpoint.
18.decisionCue: Only a validated model should reach an endpoint.

18.title: Cost and availability architecture
18.imageBrief: Cost drivers grouped by indexing, requests, output tokens and storage; Region availability gate.
learningNotes: Account for ingestion, storage, inference tokens and data transfer
Choose provisioned/throughput options only after workload measurement
Review model/feature/Region availability and service lifecycle
Set budgets, retries and throttling behavior for user-facing flows
A working prototype is not yet an operational cost design.
18.decisionCue: A working prototype is not yet an operational cost design.

18.title: AI architecture exam decisions
18.imageBrief: Four scenario cards each point to a selected service and one disqualifying condition.
learningNotes: Visual content moderation → Rekognition with review policy
Clinical PHI → Comprehend Medical; general sentiment → Comprehend
Existing Kendra or Forecast versus new-customer alternatives
Private source grounding → Bedrock Knowledge Bases with access controls
Read the input, requested output and customer availability.
18.decisionCue: Read the input, requested output and customer availability.

19.title: Agentic AI changes the trust boundary
19.imageBrief: User to agent; model proposes tool call; policy gate and optional human approval precede tool, then observation returns to agent.
learningNotes: A model proposes actions; the application and tools perform them
Separate user, agent, model, retrieval, tool and protected data roles
Every tool call crosses an authorization and data boundary
Human approval is a control for consequential actions
A model suggestion is not authorization.
19.decisionCue: A model suggestion is not authorization.

19.title: Bedrock Agent orchestration loop
19.imageBrief: Question→agent→model decision; branch to knowledge base or action group; observation loops back; final response exits.
learningNotes: InvokeAgent can use preprocessing and orchestration
The agent may retrieve knowledge, request missing parameters or invoke an action group
A tool result becomes an observation that informs another iteration
The session returns a response after sufficient evidence
An agent can iterate; it is not a fixed three-step pipeline.
19.decisionCue: An agent can iterate; it is not a fixed three-step pipeline.

19.title: Action groups are executable contracts
19.imageBrief: Agent action group schema→parameter validation→Lambda OR return-control application executor→business system.
learningNotes: Define function or API parameters in action-group schema
Fulfillment can use Lambda or return control to the application
Validate types, resource IDs, tenancy and business rules in the executor
Use least privilege and idempotent handling for retries
The tool implementation enforces the contract.
19.decisionCue: The tool implementation enforces the contract.

19.title: Knowledge retrieval is not tool permission
19.imageBrief: Parallel retrieval read lane and action write lane; explicit authorization gate before write.
learningNotes: Knowledge Bases return scoped evidence for grounding
Action groups can change external state
Retrieved content is untrusted input, not an instruction to bypass controls
Separate read access from write capability and track provenance
A document cannot grant the agent new privileges.
19.decisionCue: A document cannot grant the agent new privileges.

19.title: Agent service role and Lambda permission
19.imageBrief: Four identities with labeled permissions, not one universal role.
learningNotes: Bedrock Agents service role needs only approved model, KB and action integration access
Action-group Lambda needs a resource policy permitting the agent to invoke it
Lambda execution role separately scopes downstream actions
Caller needs InvokeAgent on intended alias
Permission to invoke a tool differs from the tool’s own permissions.
19.decisionCue: Permission to invoke a tool differs from the tool’s own permissions.

19.title: Return control keeps execution in the app
19.imageBrief: Agent→application invocationInputs; app policy/approval→external API; app result→agent via sessionState; denied branch returns no execution.
learningNotes: RETURN_CONTROL sends elicited parameters and invocationId to the application
Application checks policy and approval before executing an API
Submit the result with matching invocationId and action group in a later InvokeAgent request
Handle denial, timeout and replay explicitly
Return control makes the application the execution boundary.
19.decisionCue: Return control makes the application the execution boundary.

19.title: User confirmation before high-impact action
19.imageBrief: Proposed action→confirmation→allowed branch→fresh validation→tool; denied branch→safe response.
learningNotes: Configure confirmation for selected Bedrock Agent action-group functions
Present exact target, parameters and consequence to the user
Deny must prevent the action; never execute first and ask later
Revalidate authorization and resource state after approval
Approval belongs before the side effect.
19.decisionCue: Approval belongs before the side effect.

19.title: AgentCore Identity: inbound and outbound
19.imageBrief: Caller identity→AgentCore inbound→agent; separate outbound credential provider→tool.
learningNotes: Inbound auth verifies who may invoke the runtime or gateway
Outbound credentials enable scoped access to AWS or third-party tools
User-delegated and machine-to-machine credentials serve different ownership models
Avoid embedding long-lived API keys in prompts or agent code
Authentication into an agent does not authorize every tool.
19.decisionCue: Authentication into an agent does not authorize every tool.

19.title: Gateway authorization before tool calls
19.imageBrief: Agent→authenticated Gateway→policy decision→tool target; denied branch stops before target.
learningNotes: AgentCore Gateway exposes governed tool targets
IAM or JWT protects entry; a policy engine can authorize tool actions
Default deny and caller/resource conditions limit tool reach
Keep schema validation and downstream permissions in place
One governed gateway does not remove downstream checks.
19.decisionCue: One governed gateway does not remove downstream checks.

19.title: Three identities in delegated tool access
19.imageBrief: User principal→agent identity→credential provider→external tool, each with explicit scope.
learningNotes: Distinguish end user, agent workload and outbound service credential
Preserve caller context where the pattern supports it
Use dedicated scopes, consent and expiry for external SaaS access
Audit who requested and which credential executed the operation
A shared agent role can hide the real requester without context propagation.
19.decisionCue: A shared agent role can hide the real requester without context propagation.

19.title: Guardrails evaluate input and output
19.imageBrief: User input→input guardrail→model→output guardrail→response; blocked branches explicit.
learningNotes: Configure content, denied topic, word and sensitive-information policies
Input and output intervention behavior differs
A guardrail can attach to supported agent/model paths
Test policy versions with representative prompts and responses
A guardrail is one layer, not an access policy.
19.decisionCue: A guardrail is one layer, not an access policy.

19.title: Prompt injection crosses a data boundary
19.imageBrief: Attacker document→retrieval→agent; attempted tool call→policy/approval gate denies.
learningNotes: An attacker can place instructions in retrieved documents or tool results
Treat those bytes as data even when the model reads them
Use scoped retrieval, output checks, tool authorization and confirmation
Test exfiltration and unintended action attempts
Untrusted content must not become tool authority.
19.decisionCue: Untrusted content must not become tool authority.

19.title: Automated reasoning has a narrow proof scope
19.imageBrief: Response→policy logic check→structured feedback; separate prompt-attack filter and human review.
learningNotes: Policy-backed checks can flag contradiction and unstated assumptions
Validation is limited to variables represented in the policy
It does not detect prompt injection or off-topic material
Current documented limitations include English US and no streaming
A valid policy result is not a universal truth guarantee.
19.decisionCue: A valid policy result is not a universal truth guarantee.

19.title: Responsible AI is a lifecycle
19.imageBrief: Design→test→release gate→monitor→revise loop, with human owner at each decision.
learningNotes: Define intended use, affected users and unacceptable harms
Evaluate accuracy, harmful content, bias and privacy on representative cases
Monitor incidents and drift after release
Assign owners, version evidence and escalation paths
Safety needs continuous measurement and ownership.
19.decisionCue: Safety needs continuous measurement and ownership.

19.title: Human review must be meaningful
19.imageBrief: Agent proposal→reviewer evidence panel→approve/reject/revise; only approved path reaches executor.
learningNotes: Show source evidence, proposed action, target and impact
Reviewer can approve, reject or request more information
Record decision, identity, time and policy version
Protect against rubber-stamping, stale context and dual-control bypass
A click without context is not effective oversight.
19.decisionCue: A click without context is not effective oversight.

19.title: Step Functions approval with callback
19.imageBrief: State machine→wait for callback→approved action OR rejected close; timeout branch escalates.
learningNotes: A Standard workflow can pause using a callback task token
Deliver approval request through an application/notification channel
Authorized decision returns the token and outcome
Set timeout, denial, duplicate and expired-token behavior
The workflow must resume only from an authorized callback.
19.decisionCue: The workflow must resume only from an authorized callback.

19.title: Approval and automation need failure boundaries
19.imageBrief: Failure branches around approval token, validation, executor, and audit record.
learningNotes: Expired approval must not trigger execution
Retries must avoid duplicate side effects
Changed target state requires fresh pre-action validation
Record partial failures and compensating or manual recovery
Approval of old parameters is not approval of changed reality.
19.decisionCue: Approval of old parameters is not approval of changed reality.

19.title: Agent trace and protected evidence
19.imageBrief: Agent runtime→trace; API→CloudTrail; business approval→protected audit store, distinct evidence streams.
learningNotes: InvokeAgent traces show orchestration, KB queries and action group steps when enabled
CloudTrail records supported API activity; application logs record business decisions
AgentCore telemetry settings vary by resource and signal
Redact secrets and protect prompt, tool and trace data
A trace explains a path; it is not an access-control boundary.
19.decisionCue: A trace explains a path; it is not an access-control boundary.

19.title: Choose agent or deterministic workflow
19.imageBrief: Three independent patterns: direct API, agent selection, deterministic workflow; combined handoff for controlled execution.
learningNotes: Use an agent when open-ended interpretation and tool selection are required
Use Step Functions for known, durable and auditable state transitions
Combine them: agent proposes, workflow validates and obtains approval
Bound latency, cost, retries and blast radius
Do not make a deterministic approval process depend on model discretion.
19.decisionCue: Do not make a deterministic approval process depend on model discretion.

19.title: Walkthrough: deny injected export request
19.imageBrief: Query→retrieval with injected instruction→proposed export→deny gate; no tool execution.
learningNotes: Retrieved document contains malicious export instruction
Agent tries to propose an external tool call
Gateway policy and app validation deny unauthorized destination
Trace records attempt; user receives grounded answer without export
The data source cannot rewrite the tool policy.
19.decisionCue: The data source cannot rewrite the tool policy.

19.title: Walkthrough: approve a scoped refund
19.imageBrief: Proposal→policy→review callback→fresh validation→refund API→receipt; denial/timeout separate.
learningNotes: Agent proposes exact account, amount and refund reason
Policy caps and reviewer context determine approval
Step Functions callback pauses before executor
Executor rechecks order and idempotency; audit captures outcome
The approved payload must match the executed payload.
19.decisionCue: The approved payload must match the executed payload.

19.title: Walkthrough: investigate an agent denial
19.imageBrief: Caller→agent→gateway→tool with four diagnostic checkpoints; no automatic blanket grant.
learningNotes: Inspect caller authentication and resource policy first
Review Gateway policy denial and outbound credential scope
Compare trace, request ID and target service rejection
Fix the narrowest missing permission and retest denied paths
A tool error is not always a model problem.
19.decisionCue: A tool error is not always a model problem.

20.title: IaC makes architecture repeatable
20.imageBrief: Source template→validation→change set→regional stack; separate integration cards for Beanstalk, Service Catalog, SAM.
learningNotes: Template describes intended resources and dependencies
CloudFormation creates and updates stacks in one account/Region
Reuse across accounts/Regions needs deployment strategy and parameter differences
Elastic Beanstalk, Service Catalog and SAM can use CloudFormation underneath
A template is desired state; deployment is a controlled operation.
20.decisionCue: A template is desired state; deployment is a controlled operation.

20.title: Read the stack before updating it
20.imageBrief: Current template+proposed template→change set preview→approval→execute→events and verification.
learningNotes: Review proposed Add, Modify, Remove and possible replacement
Change set preview does not guarantee success or complete property-level effects
Check resources with data, IAM changes and service quotas
Execute after approval and monitor stack events/rollback
Preview replacements before they can destroy state.
20.decisionCue: Preview replacements before they can destroy state.

20.title: DeletionPolicy protects the old resource
20.imageBrief: Resource removal branches Delete, Retain, Snapshot; separate replace path governed by UpdateReplacePolicy.
learningNotes: Delete default applies unless exception or explicit policy
Retain leaves resource and charges; Snapshot only for supported types
RDS DBCluster and standalone DBInstance default Snapshot
S3 bucket delete requires empty bucket
DeletionPolicy does not protect a replaced physical resource.
20.decisionCue: DeletionPolicy does not protect a replaced physical resource.

20.title: Replacement requires a second policy
20.imageBrief: Old DB v1→replacement v2; UpdateReplacePolicy controls old v1; stack deletion policy controls v2 later.
learningNotes: UpdateReplacePolicy controls the old physical resource on replacement
DeletionPolicy handles stack deletion/removal, not replacement
Choose Retain or Snapshot where supported for data-bearing resources
Test endpoint changes and restore before changing identity
Replacement and deletion are different events.
20.decisionCue: Replacement and deletion are different events.

20.title: Custom resources extend a stack
20.imageBrief: CloudFormation→custom resource provider→external API or S3 cleanup→response to stack; failure/rollback branch.
learningNotes: Custom resource receives Create, Update and Delete requests
Lambda or another provider executes unsupported or external operations
Provider reports success/failure and stable physical ID
Handle timeout, retries, rollback and idempotent delete
A custom resource can block a stack if it never responds.
20.decisionCue: A custom resource can block a stack if it never responds.

20.title: StackSets deploy across accounts and Regions
20.imageBrief: Administration account StackSet→two account boxes each with Region instances; permission mode gate.
learningNotes: Administrator defines StackSet and target instances
Self-managed needs administrator/execution roles; service-managed uses Organizations integration
Choose Regions, account/OU targets and operation preferences
A StackSet is regional even when it deploys to many Regions
A StackSet is not a globally self-healing stack.
20.decisionCue: A StackSet is not a globally self-healing stack.

20.title: Automatic OU enrollment has a boundary
20.imageBrief: OU membership changes→StackSet automatic operation→new/removed stack instance; failure status route.
learningNotes: Service-managed permissions can auto-deploy to new target OU accounts
Removal/move can trigger delete or retain behavior per configuration
New accounts use StackSet defaults, not prior overrides
Monitor failed instances, concurrency and failure tolerance
Enrollment must be configured and monitored.
20.decisionCue: Enrollment must be configured and monitored.

20.title: Drift compares template and actual state
20.imageBrief: Template expected SG source /32 versus live 0.0.0.0/0→drift report→controlled remediation.
learningNotes: Manual change can diverge from a template without automatic prevention
Detect stack or resource drift for supported types/properties
Review expected versus actual configuration and remediation safety
A successful stack status does not prove in-sync resources
Drift detection observes; it does not itself block a manual change.
20.decisionCue: Drift detection observes; it does not itself block a manual change.

20.title: Secrets Manager references at deploy time
20.imageBrief: Secret in Secrets Manager→dynamic reference resolution→RDS property; rotation path distinct from stack update.
learningNotes: CloudFormation can reference a secret value without embedding it in template
Secrets Manager owns secret and rotation lifecycle
Runtime application/database integration must consume rotated value appropriately
Protect resolution permissions, logs and replacement-sensitive properties
A rotated secret is not automatically a new CloudFormation deployment.
20.decisionCue: A rotated secret is not automatically a new CloudFormation deployment.

20.title: Import an existing resource safely
20.imageBrief: Existing S3 bucket+whole-stack template+identifier→IMPORT change set→managed stack→drift check.
learningNotes: Manual import template describes whole stack and target resource
Provide resource identifier and DeletionPolicy for imported item
Import must not create/delete/change other resources in same operation
After import run drift detection; one resource cannot belong to two stacks in same Region
Import changes management ownership, not the resource identity.
20.decisionCue: Import changes management ownership, not the resource identity.

20.title: Automatic import has narrower rules
20.imageBrief: Two alternative import lanes with distinct prerequisites; converge on managed stack and drift check.
learningNotes: Auto-import needs supported type with static custom name and identifier
DeletionPolicy must be Retain or RetainExceptOnCreate
Manual import accepts any valid DeletionPolicy for imported resource
Neither path should assume arbitrary resource types are supported
Check import method prerequisites before writing the template.
20.decisionCue: Check import method prerequisites before writing the template.

20.title: Service Catalog separates admin and user
20.imageBrief: Admin→product version→portfolio+constraints→authorized user→provisioned product.
learningNotes: Admin authors versioned approved product and portfolio
IAM grants end users portfolio/product access
Launch constraint can use scoped provisioning role
User launches provisioned product with approved configuration
Portal access and provisioning authority are distinct.
20.decisionCue: Portal access and provisioning authority are distinct.

20.title: Constrain a self-service product
20.imageBrief: Portfolio permissions and launch role both feed product launch; blocked branch for disallowed parameters.
learningNotes: Product template or supported Terraform artifact is not the entire policy
Portfolio association, access and constraints shape allowed launches
Provisioning role scopes actual resource creation
Review tags, parameters, updates and termination behavior
A catalog product can still be unsafe if its launch role is broad.
20.decisionCue: A catalog product can still be unsafe if its launch role is broad.

20.title: SAM is a CloudFormation transform
20.imageBrief: SAM template→transform/synthesized CloudFormation resources→stack; local test loop separate.

20.decisionCue: SAM reduces boilerplate; CloudFormation remains the deployment engine.

20.decisionCue: A traffic shift needs measurable rollback conditions.

20.title: CDK synthesizes before deployment
20.imageBrief: CDK app→construct tree→synth template/assets→CloudFormation→AWS resources.

cdk synth outputs CloudFormation template and assets

20.decisionCue: CDK code is not directly executed by CloudFormation.

20.title: Choose CloudFormation, SAM or CDK

CDK uses programming constructs and synthesizes templates

20.decisionCue: Pick authoring experience independently from governance.

20.title: Validate policy before execution
20.imageBrief: Source→lint/Guard→change set→Hook policy gate→stack→Config drift/evaluation; distinguish stages.
learningNotes: Schema/lint and tests catch template mistakes

Hooks can warn or fail stack operations when configured

20.decisionCue: A local Guard check is not an enforced deployment gate unless wired in.

20.imageBrief: Two small YAML-like resource examples→Guard PASS/FAIL→build decision.
learningNotes: Require S3 encryption and disallow open SSH in templates
Test rules on both compliant and noncompliant fixtures
Run validation in build and preserve output with deployment revision

20.decisionCue: An untested policy can reject good stacks or miss bad ones.

20.imageBrief: Change set execution→configured Hook evaluates→warn or fail→resource operation only if permitted.
learningNotes: Hook target/action/filter controls where validation runs
